articles.title: Judge refuses to budge on order against federal prosecutor
articles.summary: (The Center Square) – A federal judge has declined to pause an earlier ruling that found Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as the top federal prosecutor in...
articles.body:
(The Center Square) – A federal judge has declined to pause an earlier ruling that found Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles.

That sets the stage for the removal of Essayli from two criminal cases next Monday unless an appellate court intervenes.

Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright rejected a request from the U.S. Department of Justice to stay his October order. Seabright ruled the government failed to demonstrate it would suffer specific harm and faces a low likelihood of success on appeal to the San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

While DOJ attorneys argued the legal dispute could potentially affect up to 5,000 prosecutions, Seabright dismissed the projection as an unsupported assertion.

The legal challenge centers on the procedures used to keep Essayli in office without U.S. Senate confirmation, which is generally required for U.S. attorneys. After reaching a 120-day statutory limit as interim U.S. attorney in 2025, Essayli resigned from the post. Then-Attorney General Pam Bondi subsequently appointed him as a "special attorney" and "first assistant U.S. attorney," an arrangement that allowed Essayli to continue leading the office without a Senate confirmation vote.

Seabright's decision aligns with a recent ruling by the 9th Circuit that invalidated a similar appointment mechanism used in Nevada for prosecutor Sigal Chattah. Legal analysts have noted that the ruling could trigger broader challenges to Essayli's authority across other federal prosecutions in the Central District of California.

The Center Square reached out to Essayli, the White House and DOJ for comment, but did not receive a response.

Hans von Spakovsky, a senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom , criticized the judicial rulings and attributed the appointment disputes to confirmation delays in Congress.

"This would not be an issue if Democrats were not doing everything they could to prevent executive branch nominees from being confirmed and Senate Republicans had made that a priority," von Spakovsky told The Center Square in an email.

Looking ahead to the incoming Congress in 2027, von Spakovsky predicted further gridlock over DOJ nominations.

"With Democrats taking over in the Senate in January, I have no doubt they will do everything they can to prevent anyone from getting confirmed, particularly U.S. Attorneys, so they can hamper the ability of the Justice Department to do its job," he said. He added opponents aim to restrict enforcement of immigration laws and civil rights oversight in states such as California.

Von Spakovsky also argued that federal courts have applied inconsistent standards regarding unconfirmed DOJ officials across different presidential administrations.

"These judges seem to have partial amnesia," said von Spakovsky , who served as counsel to the assistant attorney general for civil rights at the DOJ from 2002 to 2005. "Vanita Gupta served as the unconfirmed assistant attorney general of the Civil Rights Division at DOJ for three years during the Obama administration. No judge ever questioned her position or her authority or the validity of lawsuits she authorized, including unjustified criminal prosecutions of abortion protesters under the FACE Act."

The dispute over the Trump administration's appointment authority is expected to reach the nation's highest court. The Trump administration has petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court to review the 9th Circuit's Nevada ruling, contending that federal statutes authorize the attorney general to delegate the powers of a vacant office in this manner. Essayli has similarly maintained that the Supreme Court will resolve the matter.

articles.title: Hillary Clinton dismisses Democratic leadership battle as a 'performance' as Schumer faces progressive revolt
articles.summary: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton called Sen. Chris Van Hollen's challenge to Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader a "performance."
articles.body:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton dismissed the leadership challenge mounted by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., against Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for Senate majority leader when Democrats take control in January as a "performance."

During Clinton and co-host Kara Swisher's podcast, "High Stakes," Wednesday, Swisher asked the former secretary of state what she thought of Van Hollen's leadership challenge to Schumer. Clinton argued Democrats were elected because voters wanted changes in their own lives, not necessarily a change in Senate or House leadership.

"So, this leadership battle, to me, is kind of performance, in a way," Clinton said. "Because if you think that the majority leader of the Senate is going to replace the voices of people like James Talarico or Abdul El-Sayed or Annie Andrews, you don't know what is going to happen in the Senate.

"The majority leader will work to get legislation up, and he'll say, 'OK, Abdul, you want to put in Medicare-for-all, and Adam Hamilton, that's not your preferred approach. You work with the legislative team here to come up with your, and let's figure out how we're going to get something passed.'"

Van Hollen announced Nov. 12 that he would challenge Schumer , citing the midterm election results as a call for change.

Earlier in the discussion, Clinton said the Senate leadership election should be an open process but argued that the majority leader wasn't really the "messenger."

"I think anybody has a right to challenge the leadership of their party," she said. "I mean, it's — it should be an open process. And you know, I know Chris and have worked with him, but at this point, from my perspective, the majority leader is not the messenger. How many times did you see John Thune on television defending or espousing a message?

"Their job is different," Clinton continued. "Their job is to push the committees, to mark up legislation, get it on the floor, get it passed, get it to the House, get it to the White House.

"I want somebody who knows the ins and outs of the Senate," she said. "And just because you've been in the Senate doesn't mean that you have the, you know, hands-on experience or the team in place to really pull those parliamentary levers."

Swisher asked, "So you think it's kind of performative?" Clinton said yes.

Swisher also asked whether Schumer would survive the challenge from Van Hollen.

Republican strategist Liz Mair told Fox News Digital, "The primary tasks of Senate majority leader are corralling votes to advance or stop legislation and literal vote counting to ensure the priorities of a caucus are advanced and agenda items they oppose are thwarted, with a healthy spoonful of good fundraising and steering of committee dollars to win tough races, something Schumer did pretty well this cycle.

"His [Van Hollen's] campaign for leader apparently being all about supposed virtue signaling to the hard left on pet policies as opposed to his ability to perform the fundamentals of the job is why he's likely to lose this contest."

Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade as both minority and majority leader, so far has 15 senators in his camp, according to previous Fox News Digital reporting.

The longtime Democratic leader has remained confident, but quiet, about his chances of retaining his job, posting shortly after Van Hollen's announcement last week that he welcomed "discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader."

Van Hollen's base of support includes Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., who caucuses with Senate Democrats; Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., and Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, both progressives whom Schumer did not initially back in their respective races.

Van Hollen's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News' Alex Miller contributed to this report.

articles.title: Lula exonera Wellington Dias, ministro do Desenvolvimento Social  | G1
articles.standfirst: A exoneração foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União (DOU). De acordo com a publicação, o desligamento da pasta ocorre a pedido de Dias. Em nota, o ministério disse que o afastamento da pasta é temporário.
articles.summary: A exoneração foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União (DOU). De acordo com a publicação, o desligamento da pasta ocorre a pedido de Dias. Em nota, o ministério disse que o afastamento da pasta é temporário.
articles.body:
Ministro do Desenvolvimento Social Wellington Dias ao lado do presidente Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) exonerou o Wellington Dias do cargo de ministro do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS).

A exoneração foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União (DOU). De acordo com a publicação, o desligamento da pasta ocorre a pedido de Dias.

Em março de 2022, Dias deixou o cargo de governador do Piauí para disputar uma vaga para o Senado. Foi eleito senador, mas se licenciou para assumir o ministério no terceiro mandato de Lula.

Ele retorna para o Senado, uma vez que seu mandato termina somente em 2031.

Em nota, o MDS informou que a exoneração é temporária para "o cumprimento de compromissos parlamentares no Senado Federal, relacionados à destinação de emendas parlamentares".

Ainda de acordo com o ministério, "o retorno do ministro à pasta está previsto para a próxima semana, conforme alinhamento já realizado com a Presidência da República".

Entre outras atribuições, o ministério é responsável pela gestão do programa Bolsa Família, que virou tema da campanha à presidência da República.

A poucos dias do primeiro turno das eleições, o presidente anunciou o reajuste do benefício. A correção dos benefícios foi em cerca de 15,04%. Com isso, o piso do programa passou de R$ 600 para R$ 691.

"Eu nunca conversei com ninguém sobre ministro. É uma coisa minha. Dizem: 'Fulano vai pra tal lugar, ou vai pra outro lugar'. O cara vai inventando mentira para criar especulação (...) Cada ministério desse país será indicado por mim, na hora que eu quiser, no dia que eu quiser, e na data que eu quiser. Eu não tenho pressa, eu nem pude ainda festejar a minha vitória", disse o petista.

O petista deu a declaração durante cerimônia de regulamentação da escala 5x2, no Palácio do Planalto.

Desde o resultado das urnas, Lula tem sido pressionado a apresentar os ministros do próximo governo.

articles.title: Orla de Santos terá obras de revitalização até 2028 | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto prevê a recuperação de 21 km de vias e a renovação de 20 km de calçadas. Obras começam na segunda-feira (23), vão interditar avenidas e alterar as rotas dos ônibus municipais.
articles.summary: Com investimento de R$ 183 milhões, a revitalização da orla de Santos renovará 21 km de vias e calçadas, com foco em acessibilidade e drenagem até 2028.
articles.body:
Santos tem o maior jardim de orla do mundo — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

A Prefeitura de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, dará início às obras do programa Santos Mais , que deve revitalizar cinco principais avenidas da cidade, incluindo toda a orla, a partir da próxima segunda-feira (23). Com investimento de R$ 183,6 milhões , o projeto prevê a recuperação de 21 km de vias, a renovação de 20 km de calçadas, além de melhorias na infraestrutura.

As intervenções contemplarão as avenidas Presidente Wilson, Vicente de Carvalho e Bartolomeu de Gusmão, na orla, até a Rua Carlos de Campos, além das avenidas Bernardino de Campos (canal 2) e Ana Costa. De acordo com a Prefeitura de Santos, o programa é o maior projeto de revitalização de cinco dos principais eixos de circulação de veículos da cidade.

Os trabalhos serão divididos em etapas, com conclusão prevista para abril de 2028 . A primeira fase contempla a avenida Presidente Wilson, no trecho entre o Canal 1 e a Rua Almirante Custódio de Melo. As obras ocorrerão no sentido Ponta da Praia.

Segundo a prefeitura, as obras na orla ficarão suspensas durante a temporada de verão, a partir de 18 de dezembro, para reduzir os impactos no turismo. Elas serão retomadas em 31 de janeiro, quando também serão iniciadas as intervenções na Avenida Ana Costa.

Já a região da Avenida Bernardino de Campos deve receber as primeiras obras a partir de fevereiro. A execução será dividida em trechos, com duração estimada de sete a 30 dias, dependendo da complexidade dos serviços.

Orla (Presidente Wilson, Vicente de Carvalho e Bartolomeu de Gusmão): Novembro de 2026 até Janeiro de 2028 (R$ 73,9 milhões)

Bernardino de Campos (canal 2) : Fevereiro de 2027 até Março de 2028 (R$ 49,5 milhões)

Ana Costa: Janeiro de 2027 até Abril de 2028 (R$ 60 milhões)

Os trabalhos estarão a cargo do Consórcio Santos Infraestrutura , vencedor da concorrência internacional por R$ 183,6 milhões. Do valor total, R$ 146,8 milhões são provenientes do financiamento junto ao CAF, e o restante dos cofres municipais.

Revitalização das principais avenidas de Santos começa pela orla e terá investimento de R$ 183,6 milhões — Foto: Prefeitura de Santos

Além da revitalização dos pavimentos e calçadas, também estão previstos 5 km de drenagem, o plantio de 580 árvores, a construção de 32 baias de ônibus e a instalação de 612 rampas de acessibilidade nas esquinas das calçadas.

O investimento faz parte de um programa iniciado em 2021, que envolve financiamento internacional do CAF (Banco de Desenvolvimento da América Latina e Caribe) e contrapartida da prefeitura.

Orla da praia de Santos é espaço dos mais cobiçados por construtoras — Foto: Acervo A Tribuna

A partir de segunda-feira (23), ficará interditado o trecho da avenida da orla, entre o Canal 1 e a Rua Almirante Custódio de Mello, no sentido Ponta da Praia. O desvio para os motoristas e ônibus será feito pelo Canal 1, Rua Floriano Peixoto e Canal 2, com retorno à Avenida da Praia.

A Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) recomenda utilizar a Avenida Francisco Glicério como alternativa para evitar a concentração de veículos, destacando que manterá monitoramento do trânsito 24 horas por dia, com 24 profissionais atuando diariamente nas ruas.

Mudança no trânsito para obras do programa Santos Mais — Foto: Prefeitura de Santos

Na primeira etapa, haverá restrições de estacionamento em trechos das avenidas da orla, avenida Pinheiro Machado, Floriano Peixoto e Bernardino de Campos. As proibições variam conforme o local, podendo valer 24 horas por dia ou de segunda a sábado, das 7h às 20h.

A sinalização e os painéis de mensagens variáveis orientarão os motoristas sobre as alterações e os desvios. A prefeitura também distribuirá folhetos informativos em comércios e condomínios antes de cada etapa das obras.

A Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) recomenda que os motoristas utilizem rotas alternativas sempre que possível e consultem o aplicativo Waze para acompanhar as condições do trânsito.

Frota do transporte coletivo de Santos recebe 18 novos ônibus — Foto: Francisco Arrais/Prefeitura de Santos

Um total de 23 linhas de ônibus — seis municipais e 17 intermunicipais — utilizará uma rota alternativa pela Rua Floriano Peixoto nesta primeira etapa. Para facilitar a circulação, o estacionamento será temporariamente proibido nos dois lados da via.

Quatro linhas seguirão pela Floriano Peixoto até a Avenida Ana Costa. As demais passarão pelo Canal 2 antes de retomarem o trajeto habitual pela orla. Haverá sinalização nos pontos de ônibus para orientar os passageiros sobre as mudanças.

articles.title: Agrotóxicos na União Europeia: Manifestantes jogam cinzas em comissário | G1
articles.standfirst: Protesto em cúpula sobre câncer em Bruxelas mirou proposta que acaba com a reavaliação periódica de pesticidas, inclusive do glifosato. Mais de 2 mil cientistas pedem a suspensão do texto.
articles.summary: Durante a Cúpula do Câncer, ativistas protestaram contra o fim da reavaliação de agrotóxicos na União Europeia, medida criticada por mais de 2 mil cientistas.
articles.body:
Dois manifestantes jogaram um pó cinza contra o comissário europeu da Saúde, Olivér Várhelyi, durante a Cúpula Europeia do Câncer, em Bruxelas, nesta quinta-feira (19). O protesto foi contra a proposta da Comissão Europeia que flexibiliza as regras sobre agrotóxicos.

Várhelyi se preparava para falar sobre as ações da União Europeia contra o câncer no evento nesta manhã, quando os manifestantes se aproximaram do palco e arremessaram um pó, que se parecem cinzas, contra ele.

No vídeo, que circula pelas redes sociais, uma das manifestantes diz: “Estas são as cinzas das pessoas que vocês vão matar com os pesticidas”. (Veja a imagem acima)

Foi o comissário quem apresentou a parte da proposta que trata dos agrotóxicos. Ela integra o pacote Omnibus, que elimina a revisão regular de muitas das substâncias usadas nesses produtos.

Pelas regras atuais da UE, em vigor desde 2011, os principais componentes dos pesticidas, conhecidos como substâncias ativas, só podem ser autorizados por períodos limitados, de no máximo 15 anos. A proposta da Comissão Europeia muda essa lógica.

Pelo texto, a autorização por prazo indeterminado passaria a ser a regra, inclusive para substâncias controversas como o glifosato, associado por estudos ao câncer. Revisões de segurança ocorreriam apenas em situações excepcionais.

E por que isso? A proposta da Comissão é acabar com a fila de agrotóxicos à espera de aprovação e facilitar a vida dos agricultores. Mas vem enfrentando forte oposição de especialistas e da sociedade civil.

Antes do evento, nesta quarta-feira (18), mais de 2 mil cientistas assinaram uma carta que pede a suspensão do texto até que se faça uma avaliação de impacto independente.

O grupo de defesa do consumidor Foodwatch levou o caso ao Provedor de Justiça Europeu, órgão que investiga queixas contra instituições do bloco, e acusa a Comissão de má administração.

Qual a relação entre essas substâncias e o câncer?

Agrotóxicos são substâncias consideradas potencialmente cancerígenas , mas o risco varia conforme a substância e a exposição, explica o médico oncologista Stephen Stephanini.

A Agência Internacional de Pesquisa em Câncer (IARC), ligada à Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), classifica as substâncias de acordo com a força das evidências de que podem causar a doença.

Lindano : está no Grupo 1, o das substâncias com evidência suficiente de que causam câncer.

Glifosato : está no Grupo 2A, o dos prováveis cancerígenos.

Segundo o oncologista, essa classificação aponta um perigo, mas não calcula a chance de uma pessoa específica ter câncer. A IARC diz se uma substância é capaz de provocar a doença.

Quanto isso pesa para cada um depende da dose, do tempo de exposição, da frequência e da forma de contato com o produto.

“Não há dúvida de que flexibilizar controle e supervisão gera incerteza”, explica Stephanini.

Revisões periódicas já tiraram 56 substâncias do mercado europeu

Para os críticos, o ponto central é que os efeitos nocivos de um agrotóxico costumam aparecer anos depois da aprovação, quando o produto é reavaliado à luz de estudos mais recentes.

Desde 2011, 56 substâncias ativas foram proibidas na UE em decorrência dessas revisões, segundo Salome Roynel, da ONG Pesticide Action Network Europe. Entre elas está o inseticida clorpirifós, usado em pomares, hortaliças e cereais e associado a prejuízos ao desenvolvimento cerebral de crianças.

A ecotoxicologista Martina Vijver, da Universidade de Leiden, na Holanda, afirma que a percepção dos riscos muda com o tempo. “O sistema regulatório precisa manter a capacidade de corrigir decisões tomadas ontem com o conhecimento de amanhã”, disse em audiência no Parlamento Europeu, em setembro.

A exposição da população é ampla. Um levantamento feito entre 2014 e 2021 encontrou resíduos de dois ou mais pesticidas em 84% das amostras de urina de crianças e adultos em cinco países europeus.

A Agência Europeia do Ambiente afirma que ainda não é possível calcular com precisão quantas doenças estão ligadas aos agrotóxicos. Mesmo assim, a exposição a essas substâncias, incluindo algumas já proibidas que continuam no ambiente, foi associada a diferentes tipos de câncer, doenças respiratórias crônicas, distúrbios neurológicos, atrasos no desenvolvimento infantil e problemas de fertilidade.

Em setembro, mais de 500 especialistas já haviam pedido ao Parlamento Europeu que suspendesse a análise da proposta. Em outubro, especialistas da ONU defenderam uma revisão para verificar se as mudanças respeitam as obrigações de direitos humanos do bloco, sobretudo em relação a trabalhadores rurais e crianças.

articles.title: Senado: Justiça libera gasto de R$ 6 milhões com iPhones | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão é da presidente do TRF-1, desembargadora federal Maria do Carmo Cardoso. Na quarta, liminar tinha suspendido licitação após ação do deputado Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG).
articles.summary: A decisão da presidência do TRF-1 permite que o Senado gaste R$ 6 milhões com iPhones e 675 linhas telefônicas, alegando que a suspensão prejudicaria a gestão da Casa.
articles.body:
A Justiça Federal autorizou nesta quinta-feira (19) a retomada da licitação do Senado que prevê gasto de até R$ 6 milhões com linhas telefônicas e celulares, incluindo iPhones , para senadores e servidores da Casa.

A decisão é da presidente do Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região (TRF-1). desembargadora Maria do Carmo Cardoso, e revoga a liminar que havia suspendido a licitação na quarta (18).

Com isso, o Senado pode continuar o processo e avançar para a contratação da empresa vencedora.

iPhone 18 Pro nas cores preto, glacial, prata e bordô — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

Na decisão, a desembargadora afirma que manter todo o processo parado poderia prejudicar o funcionamento administrativo do Senado e causar impacto aos cofres públicos .

A desembargadora também suspendeu a multa diária de R$ 50 mil que havia sido firmada pela primeira decisão, em caso de avanço dos contratos.

95 aparelhos de "categoria superior" – o edital prevê que sejam iPhones 18 Pro;

chips, modems, ligações e planos de roaming internacional.

O processo judicial que levou à suspensão da contratação foi movido pelo deputado federal reeleito Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG).

Na decisão provisória que suspendeu o pregão, o juiz federal Arthur Pinheiro Chaves questionou as especificações do edital, como a exigência de modelos específicos de iPhone para os parlamentares .

🤳Os aparelhos seriam fornecidos em regime de comodato — uma espécie de empréstimo — e deveriam ser substituídos após dois anos de uso. A regra valia para os celulares dos dois tipos previstos no edital: os iPhones e os modelos intermediários.

🤳A substituição após dois anos seria feita por causa da “evolução tecnológica”. No caso dos iPhones, o edital determinava que o novo aparelho fosse “o melhor aparelho da categoria 'high end' disponível para o mercado corporativo e que atenda aos requisitos técnicos estabelecidos" .

Segundo o Senado, a contratação dos serviços é "indispensável para garantir o adequado desempenho das atividades institucionais, assegurando conectividade contínua para parlamentares e servidores, em consonância com a crescente digitalização dos serviços e sistemas disponibilizados pelo Senado Federal."

articles.title: Compliance Zero: Fachin mantém prisão de Felipe Vorcaro, primo do ex-dono do Master  | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do STF negou pedido de revogação feito pela defesa e confirmou necessidade da medida. Investigado é apontado pela PF como operador financeiro de organização criminosa.
articles.summary: Presidente do STF negou pedido de revogação feito pela defesa e confirmou necessidade da medida. Investigado é apontado pela PF como operador financeiro de organização criminosa.
articles.body:
O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), ministro Edson Fachin , negou o pedido de liberdade e manteve a prisão preventiva de Felipe Vorcaro , primo de Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master. A decisão foi assinada nesta quarta-feira (18).

Felipe Vorcaro é investigado no âmbito da Operação Compliance Zero, que apura crimes contra o sistema financeiro nacional, lavagem de dinheiro, ocultação patrimonial e corrupção envolvendo agentes públicos.

Na decisão, Fachin analisou tanto o pedido de revogação da prisão preventiva apresentado pela defesa quanto a reavaliação obrigatória da necessidade da prisão a cada 90 dias, prevista na legislação penal.

Para o presidente da Corte, embora o tempo tenha passado, não houve alteração no quadro que justifique a soltura.

Fachin destacou que a medida segue indispensável para garantir a ordem, a instrução criminal e a aplicação da lei penal, diante do risco concreto de fuga e de reiteração criminosa.

Felipe Vorcaro, primo de Daniel Vorcaro, apontado como um dos envolvidos no esquema do Banco Master. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Depois da vitória no Senado, líderes governistas afirmam que Lula fará novo ajuste nas contas públicas | G1
articles.body:
O presidente brasileiro Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva conversa após reunião com o Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE) em Brasília, Brasil, em 6 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Herculano

Logo depois da vitória no Senado na votação do ajuste fiscal, líderes governistas revelaram ao blog que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) fará um novo ajuste nas contas públicas para arrumar a casa e atrair investidores ao país.

As medidas, segundo esses líderes, serão discutidas pelo presidente com o novo ministro da Fazenda, que deve ser anunciado em breve.

O governo conseguiu manter os principais pontos do ajuste fiscal elaborado pela equipe do ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti. Cedeu a governadores no repasse de recursos da antiga Lei Kandir e também ao agronegócio no uso de créditos de PIS e Cofins.

Com isso, obteve uma vitória importante no Senado.

O blog conversou com líderes próximos ao presidente Lual tão logo a sessão acabou. Eles foram direto ao ponto.

"Sabemos que esse ajuste é um primeiro passo importante, mas o presidente sabe que terá de fazer e fará um novo ajuste para arrumar a economia e atrair investidores", disse reservadamente um desses líderes.

O governo chegou a temer uma derrota na terça-feira (17), mas com negociações pontuais aprovou ontem as medidas com certa folga e manteve a potência financeira do pacote.

Segundo o ministro Bruno Moretti, o pacote vai permitir um ganho de R$ 50 bilhões, fazendo com que o país saia de um déficit primário de 0,4% do PIB neste ano para um superávit de 0,1% do PIB.

A oposição, que chegou ao plenário confiante de que derrotaria o governo em pelo menos um destaque, saiu derrotada. Líderes da oposição se queixaram que alguns senadores do seu campo acabaram votando com o governo depois das negociações feitas pelos articuladores presidenciais, principalmente com o agronegócio e governadores.

Enquanto isso, com sua reeleição encaminhada, o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), prometeu votar o ajuste fiscal no início da próxima semana.

Ele cobrou, porém, novas medidas fiscais, alertando que a dívida pública precisa cair no país. Hugo Motta e Alcolumbre estão jogando juntos para apoiar o governo Lula em seu quarto mandato.

articles.title: Lula e Alcolumbre: reunião vai debater vaga no STF e novo governo | G1
articles.summary: Davi Alcolumbre negocia com Lula a indicação de Rodrigo Pacheco ao STF e mudanças no novo governo após garantir vitórias importantes para o ajuste fiscal no Senado.
articles.body:
Depois de garantir seguidas vitórias para o governo no Senado , o presidente da Casa, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), tem um encontro com o presidente Lula previsto para os próximos dias.

Na conversa, o senador deve falar com Lula sobre o nome que indicará para o Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) ainda neste ano. Além disso, os dois vão falar sobre a montagem do novo governo a partir do ano que vem, especificamente, a cota do União Brasil no quarto mandato do petista.

Entre as vitórias do governo no Senado, a última foi a aprovação das medidas do ajuste fiscal, ocorrida nesta quarta-feira (18).

Antes, Alcolumbre havia comandado a aprovação das PECs do fim da escala 6x1 e a da Segurança Pública . O senador do Amapá busca sua recondução ao posto mais alto do Senado, e tem o apoio do presidente Lula.

Alcolumbre decidiu não viajar para o Amapá neste feriado e permanecer em Brasília aguardando o convite de Lula para uma conversa.

O presidente do Senado não esconde de ninguém que seu nome para substituir Luís Roberto Barroso continua sendo o do ex-senador Rodrigo Pacheco , atualmente ministro do Tribunal de Contas da União .

Dentro do Senado, por sinal, tanto senadores governistas como os de oposição avaliam que uma indicação de Rodrigo Pacheco seria aprovada rapidamente pela Casa, ainda neste ano. Se Lula optar por outro nome, enfrentará dificuldades.

O envio do nome de Jorge Messias novamente, como defendem alguns petistas, é classificado como senadores como um novo convite para uma derrota. Messias foi rejeitado em abril deste ano .

O presidente do Senado vai tratar também da montagem da equipe de Lula para o quarto mandato. O ministro do Desenvolvimento e Integração Nacional, Waldez Góes, indicado por Alcolumbre , perdeu apoio do senador.

Alcolumbre disse a aliados que o ministro praticamente o traiu no Estado, não fazendo campanha para seus candidatos.

Ou seja, o senador não apoia a permanência de Waldez no posto, na cota do União Brasil. O União Brasil, partido de Alcolumbre, deseja seguir ocupando três ministérios no quarto mandato de Lula.

articles.title: Strongman ‘friends,’ AI’s potential and other takeaways from Trump’s China trip and sitdown with Putin and Xi
articles.summary: Officials were frank heading into Thursday’s unprecedented three-way talks: US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin were unlikely to leave Shenzhen with any major agreements.
articles.body: Officials were frank heading into Thursday’s unprecedented three-way talks: US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin were unlikely to leave Shenzhen with any major agreements. Diplomatic breakthroughs, it turned out, were not the point. The talks themselves were the deliverable. Gathered at a round table inside a state guesthouse on the outskirts of this modern metropolis, each man cited the “responsibility” on them to jointly navigate a complicated world. “History tells us that when great powers are at peace, the world is secure; when great powers clash, the world is in chaos,” Xi said as the talks were starting. Each was also looking to gain something from the power projection the meeting afforded. For Putin, it was a chance to reemerge on the biggest global platform, with vastly more powerful nations, after being shunned nearly five years ago for his invasion of Ukraine. A joint statement released after the meeting listed immunity for state officials as “of fundamental importance,” a matter of significance for a leader who is wanted for war crimes by the International Criminal Court. Xi was able to portray himself — and China — as a diplomatic power player, even as economic problems dog him at home. And Trump, whose lame-duck era was hastened after this month’s midterm election battering, was able to show he’s still in the game with two men whose power in their own countries goes mostly unchecked. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech together,” Trump said as the meeting began. “We are choosing a different course.” “Let’s see if we can get something done,” he said before the press was dismissed and the meeting got underway. Here are five takeaways from the summit in Shenzhen. What was the point? Whether Thursday’s meeting will be remembered as a historic pivot point — or just another photo-op — isn’t yet clear. Eighty-one minutes was hardly enough time to resolve all the major differences between the three countries, on wars, economics and cutting-edge technology. Heading into the talks, the leaders’ objectives seemed to differ. The summit was initially proposed by Putin as a way to discuss the war in Ukraine without representatives from Ukraine at the table — a prospect that sent shivers through Kyiv and led to comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference, when world powers carved up the postwar world into spheres of influence. Both Xi and Putin referenced the post-World War II moment in their opening remarks as a time when powerful countries joined together to shape the world, a hint of how they viewed Thursday’s encounter. Initially, American officials said Ukraine would not be on the agenda — though Trump later said he would bring it up. “I think things are happening. I think that (Putin) and I hope the other side would like to see an end to that war,” he said at the start of the meeting. More important, in Trump’s mind, was a discussion on nuclear arms control among the world’s largest nuclear states. Trump wants to negotiate a new nonproliferation pact with Moscow and Beijing, though he was candid about the difficulties of reaching an agreement. “Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard to not have them,” he said. “It’s the way life works.” Xi has appeared uninterested in entering a nuclear agreement with two countries whose arsenals of warheads are many times the size of China’s. And he was initially reluctant to host tripartite talks at all that could overshadow his APEC summit, according to US officials. Speaking in the hours before the sit-down, Trump was asked about the advantages of meeting the two autocrats together. “They both like Trump,” he said. “Now, what happens after me? That I can’t tell you.” Relationship building The competing objectives for the summit didn’t seem to matter once the men arrived at the Kylin Villa, alongside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park. They convened at a round table, spaced apart equally with Xi in the middle. “We are really making history,” Trump said proudly. “The three of us have a great deal to discuss.” The relationships on display are complicated. Trump has worked ardently to cultivate both Xi and Putin over the last two years, hoping deeper personal ties will translate into smoother geopolitics. He’s employed flattery and showy summits to fete and elevate his counterparts. He called both men “friends” in individual meetings beforehand. “I think as long as you and I are in charge of things, we’ll never have a problem,” Trump told Xi. The flattery has yet to yield significant breakthroughs. Trump has complained his relationship with Putin, helped along by a summit in Alaska last year, has so far failed to end the Ukraine war. Disputes over trade and shipments of rare earths continue to act as irritants in the US-China relationship. And both countries are providing assistance and technology to Iran. Xi and Putin, who proclaimed five years ago they were partners “without limits,” have met dozens of times. After another meeting here on Wednesday, Chinese state media declared the relationship was “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.” Xi and Putin have long been united by a shared view that the global balance of power is undergoing a fundamental shift in their favor, as the East rises and the West is in decline. Or, said another way, that the age of the American superpower is ending. With this unprecedented three-way meeting with Trump, Xi and Putin have clinched what both are sure to use as a new, landmark testament to that view. Countries at war Two of the three men in Thursday’s meeting are embroiled in wars against smaller adversaries that have stretched on longer than anticipated. Trump’s war in Iran and Putin’s war in Ukraine have each sapped military resources and led to global price increases — and frustrated Xi, who sees the conflicts as a threat to global stability. Both wars were topics Trump hoped to discuss with Xi and Putin, each of whom maintains ties with Tehran. Trump has not applied pressure on Moscow or Beijing to cut off their ties. In fact, he loosened sanctions on Russian diesel, applied after the invasion of Ukraine, in an attempt to bring down costs that spiked as a result of the Iran war, indirectly allowing that conflict to enrich Russia. Trump has grown exasperated by all the war. The conflict in Iran, which he initially said would last six weeks, is highly unpopular at home and, by his own admission, led to sweeping Republican losses in the midterms. He is now weighing military options to restart a new, intensive round of bombing. Meanwhile, his campaign pledge to resolve the Ukraine war within 24 hours of taking office is now 667 days overdue. How much help Xi and Putin will be in ending the wars isn’t clear. And how much a summit without Ukraine or Iran at the table can do toward bringing peace seems limited. Still, Trump appeared hopeful. “A lot of people weren’t sure would something come out of it. I think something … will come out,” Trump said beforehand as he met with Xi. “I mean, very very strongly. I think something will come out.” Over in Berlin, Jared Kushner said that Trump dialed into the meeting of the “Coalition of the Willing” and gave his assessment of the talks in Shenzhen. The president’s son-in-law — speaking alongside the leaders of Germany, France, Ukraine and the United Kingdom at the summit — said Trump had conveyed “a very strong message to both of them [Xi and Putin] on the desire for peace and would like to engage both of them very aggressively to get there.” He didn’t elaborate but said Trump “came away believing that peace is achievable.” Steve Witkoff, the president’s special envoy, said that Trump had made “Ukraine and a peaceful end to this” a central part of his message in Shenzhen. Battle for AI supremacy Even before Trump arrived in Shenzhen, the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset was overshadowing the stop. So, too, were cascading service outages in the United States — caused in some cases by AI updates — causing anxiety the administration at first was slow to address. Questions of how the US will compete in the rapidly developing AI industry seemed more urgent set against the backdrop of this gleaming hub of China’s tech and chip-making. And the revelations about Huang served to expose a deep rift within Trump’s cabinet over how — or whether — to restrict the sale of high-powered AI chips to China. Sitting alongside Xi at dinner on Wednesday evening, Trump raised the matter only briefly, he said afterward. Heading to China, he said he was wary of “insulting” China by pressing the spying issue too hard. Many in his administration are more hawkish, and want to cut off China’s access to the most advanced AI chips. Trump, however, sounded opposed to any steps that could “stifle” AI’s advances. “We do not want to do anything to destroy the tremendous potential of this technology,” he said. “We oppose any form of globalist regulation.” Still, as he was speaking to Asian leaders, Trump did seem to acknowledge there could be danger ahead. “We have to be careful. We have to cherish it. It’s almost completely good, but it’s got some bad elements,” he said. “And we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements.” Xi as a diplomatic power player Beijing will see this summit as a major success for Chinese diplomacy. Trump’s praise of China and his assurances that as long as he and Xi are in charge they’ll “never have a problem” are welcome words for a Chinese leadership that’s closely watching for a tone shift in US policy toward China amid growing calls from US lawmakers to tighten controls on Chinese access to US high-tech. Beijing was clearly interested in using Trump’s visit to capitalize on the US president’s goodwill towards China — especially ahead of a change of power in Congress and as Trump enters the final leg of his final term. Xi’s precedent-breaking airport welcome of Trump and his apparent warmth toward the American president in their interactions would have been carefully calibrated with that in mind. The lack of concrete outcomes from the trilateral meeting also suited Beijing’s agenda, as Xi was widely seen to be wary of a Yalta 2.0 set of optics when it comes to discussions on the fate of Ukraine. That would have clashed with China’s avowed push for more multilateralism on the global stage. Instead, Xi got to show himself as international convener — and a powerbroker whose diplomatic stature allows it to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the US — without making any complicated commitments. That’s good timing for Xi, who is looking to bolster his own profile ahead of a key Communist Party conclave next year where’s he’s expect to cement his fourth term atop the China’s power structure.

articles.title: Lula assina decreto com regras para o fim da escala 6x1; ASSISTA
articles.summary: Transição para a jornada 5x2 está prevista para começar em 16 de dezembro, com dois dias de folga por semana e redução da carga horária sem corte salarial.
articles.body:
Transição para a jornada 5x2 está prevista para começar em 16 de dezembro, com dois dias de folga por semana e redução da carga horária sem corte salarial.

Lula assinou nesta quinta-feira (19) o decreto que regulamenta a mudança para a escala 5x2, com dois dias de descanso por semana.

A transição está prevista para 16 de dezembro de 2026, quando a jornada máxima semanal será reduzida de 44 para 42 horas.

Uma segunda etapa, prevista para 12 meses depois, reduzirá a carga horária máxima para 40 horas semanais, sem diminuição dos salários.

Os dias de descanso serão negociados em convenções coletivas. Cada setor poderá adaptar a escala à sua atividade, respeitando as oito folgas mensais e a manutenção dos salários.

Lula assina o documento que regulamenta a jornada 5x2.

O presidente Lula deve assinar nesta quinta-feira (19) o decreto que estabelece as regras do fim da escala 6x1 e a transição à jornada 5x2, com dois dias de descanso por semana. A mudança está prevista para começar em dezembro, com redução gradual da carga horária de 44 para 40 horas semanais, sem corte nos salários. O g1 transmitirá a cerimônia de assinatura ao vivo.

articles.title: Trump scores key win over House progressive accused of assaulting ICE agent
articles.summary: New Jersey Rep. LaMonica McIver says she faces 17 years in prison after the 3rd Circuit refused to reconsider her ICE charges at Delaney Hall.
articles.body: The Trump administration scored another win in court Thursday over a House progressive who was accused of assaulting federal immigration agents at a facility in New Jersey in 2025. Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., was denied her request that the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit reconsider its August 2026 decision that would have her face at least two of the three charges related to a confrontation between Democrats and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at Delaney Hall in Newark, New Jersey. McIver previously tried to invoke the Constitution's Speech or Debate Clause in order to evade the charges, but the federal court's three-judge panel denied that motion in a 2-1 decision earlier this year. Thursday's order upholds that decision. EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET "Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power — but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning. Because of a weaponized Department of Justice and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison," McIver said in a statement. "Now, due to the disappointing decision by the Third Circuit, we are all one step closer to a world in which the President of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for." McIver called the result "disappointing" and said she and her lawyers "are looking at every possible option for what comes next." WATCH: AMERICA’S FIRST ‘FORMERLY UNDOCUMENTED’ CONGRESSMAN DELIVERS ULTIMATUM AT BESIEGED ICE FACILITY An unannounced visit to the Delaney Hall detention center by a group of Democratic officials devolved into chaos in May 2025 that culminated in a physical standoff between federal lawmakers and ICE agents and the arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. McIver was charged with three counts, including assaulting and impeding federal officers. McIver initially argued that her actions fell under her constitutionally protected duties as a member of Congress and, therefore, she could not be prosecuted. But a 2-1 decision issued in August 2026 by Biden-appointed Judge Cindy Chung and Trump-appointed Judge Stephanos Bibas stated that McIver's argument of legislative immunity would not stand for two of the three counts, while the third count was sent back to a lower court for further review. Court documents say McIver allegedly "slammed her forearm" into a federal officer trying to arrest Baraka. On that count, the federal appellate court agreed with a lower court decision that her "alleged intervention into the Mayor’s questionable arrest had no cognizable connection to any legislative function" protected by the Constitution. NEW JERSEY AGITATORS BITE, KICK AND PUNCH ICE AGENTS AS DELANEY HALL CLASHES CONTINUE; 9 MORE ARRESTED: DHS The second count alleged that McIver used both of her forearms to "strike [an officer] as she returned inside of the secured area of Delaney Hall." The two judges wrote, "Like the acts charged in Count One, the acts of pushing past and forcibly striking someone are unambiguously non-legislative: they are not integral to the legislative process." Judge Thomas Ambro wrote in dissent, "When an Executive Branch official prevents a Member from entering a DHS facility, she is denied effective access to an oversight inspection." articles.title: Florida's Donalds predicts it would be ‘foolhardy’ to try recreate Trump’s coalition in 2028
articles.summary: The GOP Gov.-elect shared his thoughts about the forthcoming presidential showdown and eliminated the possibility that he might run for president in 2028.
articles.body:
Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds said he thinks it would be difficult for any Republican running for the White House in 2028 to try to recreate President Donald Trump's coalition.

"To be blunt: What I've observed in politics, it's very hard for somebody to try to recreate the previous person's coalition," Donalds told POLITICO's Adam Wren in an onstage interview at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah.

Donalds, who was on Trump's short list for vice president in 2024 and recently made history as the nation's first elected Black Republican governor, said he watched Democrats struggle to recreate former President Barack Obama's coalition. Similarly, he said, the coalitions for Trump and former President Bill Clinton belonged to them.

"Whoever the next person is going to be, they're going to have to — in some respects — redefine and reshape the electorate about what their supportive coalition is," he said. "I think trying to go back into trying to recreate what somebody else's success was, I think is foolhardy."

Asked whether the comments were specifically intended toward Vice President JD Vance, Donalds replied that it was "just the reality of politics," and that running based on the coalition someone else built "rarely" works. Every candidate, he said, has to address the latest issues, figure out how they are going to talk about them and decide how they'll allow voters to see them.

"I would advise anybody who's thinking about taking the next step: You got to define yourself," he said. "You have to be yourself. You can't be a facsimile or a carbon copy or shades of gray of somebody else."

As for Donalds himself, he said he was "absolutely" closing the door to running for president in 2028, saying he was looking forward to leaving Capitol Hill to be in Florida, which he called the "hottest thing going" in the last three decades.

"It is not happening. I am focused on Florida," Donalds said of a potential '28 run, adding that he wanted to help the state focus on "the next 30 years of growth."

"I take this job very seriously," he added. "I am not looking at another one."

As for his predecessor, Gov. Ron DeSantis — who unsuccessfully ran for the Republican nomination for president in 2024 — Donalds said it was "too early to tell" on a possible 2028 bid. But he praised the current governor's record, saying it "speaks for itself." Though he stressed he had not discussed the matter with DeSantis, he noted the two-term governor may also have family considerations at play given that his children are getting older.

"Running for office is not an easy feat, and you know, the higher you go, the more planning is involved," he said. "But I think the voters are going to make those decisions about who they want to be the standard bearer of our party or who they're going to want to be the standard bearer of the Democrat Party, and we have a long way to go."

articles.title: Judge says Rollins’s religious holiday messages likely violated First Amendment
articles.summary: A district court judge on Thursday said U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins likely violated the First Amendment after sending emails to her staff about Jesus Christ, God, Christmas and Easter. Rollins had sent out four holiday-related emails, which prompted federal employees to file a lawsuit in May. U.S. District Court Judge Trina…
articles.body:
A district court judge on Thursday said U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins likely violated the First Amendment after sending emails to her staff about Jesus Christ, God, Christmas and Easter.

Rollins had sent out four holiday-related emails, which prompted federal employees to file a lawsuit in May. U.S. District Court Judge Trina Thompson agreed with the employees on the emails referring to Christmas and Easter.

Thompson issued a preliminary injunction blocking Rollins from sending out faith-laden emails. The Biden-appointed judge wrote in her ruling that Rollins’s “good faith intentions … are not the issue here.”

“The April 5, 2026, and Dec. 23, 2025, messages go too far,” Thompson wrote. “They suggest acquiescence that amounts to coercive pressure; a pressure of conformity sufficient to raise an Establishment Clause violation.”

She elaborated that protecting “private devotion and spiritual reflection from government influence comes to the fore.”

“The wisdom of the Founders was in recognizing that independence requires freedom of conscience,” she continued. “The command of the Establishment Clause, thus, is to prohibit the government from using its authority to try to sway an individual’s decision about whether and how to practice their faith … this court requires the Secretary to observe her own directives.”

The Easter email told USDA employees that God had “granted each of us victory and new life. And where there is life –– risen life –– there is hope.” The email begins with “Happy Easter — He is Risen indeed!”

Thompson said the comparison between employees and “the very first disciples to encounter our risen Lord in the Upper Room almost two thousand years ago” portrays “the agency’s work as a mission to serve her particular Christian views.”

The Hill has reached out to the USDA for comment.

Politico first reported on the Easter message earlier this year, when USDA employees claimed the messages made them “feel excluded and unwelcome, and they fear the negative consequences of not sharing the Secretary’s religion or expressing their own different beliefs in the workplace.”

The employees were represented by Americans United for Separation of Church and State, Democracy Forward and Bryan Schwartz Law.

Americans United president and CEO Rachel Laser said in a statement that the decision should send a message to the Trump administration “that it cannot misuse taxpayer resources to preach, hold government-sponsored prayer services during work time and broadcast Christian Nationalism over official communication channels. Not on our watch.”

“I am heartened and relieved to see the court upholding the Constitution and protecting employees from further inappropriate messages from the secretary,” USDA employee Ashley Miller said in a statement from Democracy Forward. “It was quite scary to come forward, but I am proud we did so, knowing this will help everyone across USDA.”

Rollins has been very open about her Christian faith, posting excerpts of Scripture on social media. She also takes part in Bible study groups with other Trump administration Cabinet members.

The Establishment Clause of the First Amendment prohibits the federal government from establishing any official religion or showing preference to any one religion over others. It was also established to prohibit state-sponsored churches like the Church of England, according to the U.S. Courts website.

The amendment’s Free Exercise Clause protects people’s right to practice their own religion as long as it does not run afoul of a “compelling” governmental interest, as cited by the 1944 Prince v. Massachusetts decision. The Supreme Court ruled at the time that the state could force children to be inoculated despite parents citing their faith as against inoculation.

articles.title: Fiona the Hippo dies days after ingesting hat, Cincinnati Zoo announces
articles.summary: The zoo announced Fiona’s death Thursday afternoon on social media.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI ( WDTN ) – Fiona the Hippo has died after eating a hat that ended up in her enclosure by accident, the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Gardens.

The zoo announced Fiona’s death Thursday afternoon on social media.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” reads a message the zoo posted to Facebook.

“The vet staff tried everything they could to help her after she ingested a hat that ended up in her habitat by accident last week. Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover.”

The zoo had explained several days ago that a visitor had accidentally tossed the hat into Fiona’s habitat. ( NewsNation reported that the hat hit a ceiling fan before going into the hippo’s enclosure.) The staff was “cautiously optimistic” that Fiona would pass the hat on her own and monitored her around the clock.

In their latest post, they asked Fiona’s fans to “keep her keepers and everyone who tried to help her” in their thoughts.

“We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are.”

After the initial incident, zoo staffers warned visitors to keep their personal items secure, and to alert a worker if any potentially harmful objects ended up in the enclosures.

Fiona, 9, was born Jan. 24, 2017 to Bibi and Henry. Her half-brother, Fritz, was born in 2022.

articles.title: House Ethics Committee adopts rule changes around sexual misconduct investigations
articles.summary: The House Ethics Committee voted Thursday to adopt a collection of rule changings seeking to expedite sexual misconduct investigations within the lower chamber and increase transparency throughout the process. The panel unanimously passed the changes, which include granting its leadership subpoena authority, streamlining deadlines for respondents to address an investigative subcommittee’s findings and codifying its…
articles.body:
The House Ethics Committee voted Thursday to adopt a collection of rule changings seeking to expedite sexual misconduct investigations within the lower chamber and increase transparency throughout the process.

The panel unanimously passed the changes, which include granting its leadership subpoena authority, streamlining deadlines for respondents to address an investigative subcommittee’s findings and codifying its “policy of publicly disclosing any findings that a Member engaged in sexual harassment or other sexual misconduct.”

“We believe that these rule changes will provide more transparency. They will expedite our investigative process while maintaining protections for witnesses and victims, while also making sure that the process for the members themselves who are under the purview of this committee, that that due process is protected,” Rep. Michael Guest (R-Miss.), who chairs the committee, said in the public session before the vote.

Lawmakers from both parties have called for faster Ethics Committee investigations into sexual misconduct as a string of high-profile cases involving House members intensified scrutiny of the panel’s often-secretive process.

One of the more recent prominent cases involved outgoing Rep. Cory Mills (R-Fla.), whose ex-girlfriend accused him of harassment and threatening to release explicit images of her. Another woman Mills dated initially told police he assaulted her in February 2025 before recanting.

Mills, who is leaving his post in January after losing in his state’s GOP primary, has denied all allegations of wrongdoing. The Ethics panel has been investigating him since November 2025.

The Ethics Committee also said earlier this year it was investigating reports that Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) violated House rules by “engaging in inappropriate sexual contact with a House staffer.” Gomez told The Hill in an August statement his actions “were consensual in nature and haven’t violated the law or House Ethics rules.”

Former Reps. Tony Gonzales (R-Texas) and Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.), who had both been accused of sexual misconduct, were under investigation when pressure to resign from both sides of the aisle contributed to their departures from Congress in April.

And more recently, House lawmakers voted to censure Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) in September after a damning Ethics report found he demonstrated “persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers.” Edwards dropped his midterm reelection bid after the panel released its findings.

Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-Calif.), the House Ethics Committee’s ranking member, said he hopes the rule changes will reinforce the committee’s “commitment to the integrity of the House of Representatives on sexual harassment.”

“We’re hoping that all of these changes will reflect positively on the committee, and they should, and our staff, but also in the House as we do these improvements and look at further ways to make sure that the process is fair, transparent, and people are held accountable,” he added.

articles.title: Trump gives posthumous pardon to Pete Rose, all-time MLB hits leader
articles.summary: The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games.
articles.body: President Donald Trump announced on social media Thursday that he has pardoned the late Pete Rose, baseball’s all-time hits leader. “I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND, whose record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social as he was returning from a meeting in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Rose had 4,256 hits in his major league career, not in a single season. Trump’s post was later edited to correct that achievement. Trump added that Rose “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame.” Rose died in 2024 at age 83. He pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been permanently banned from baseball after he gambled on his own team as a player and manager. That ban was posthumously lifted last year after repeated requests from Trump. MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said at the time that permanent ineligibility “ends upon the passing of the disciplined individual.” Trump, who’d advocated for Rose’s inclusion in the Baseball Hall of Fame for years, announced his plans to pardon Rose in March 2025. “He never betted against himself, or the other team. He had the most hits, by far, in baseball history, and won more games than anyone in sports history,” Trump said then. Rose denied he’d gambled on baseball for almost 15 years before admitting in his 2004 autobiography that he’d bet both as a player and a manager, but never against his own team. Rose played 24 seasons in Major League Baseball, the last three as a player-manager for the Cincinnati Reds, where he played for the bulk of his career. The National Baseball Hall of Fame has said that Rose’s removal from the ineligible list means his candidacy can be considered when its Classic Baseball Era Committee meets in December of next year.

articles.title: Justice Department urges federal judge to let 2-year Kennedy Center closure go forward
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday defended a decision by the Kennedy Center board to shutter the performing arts center for a planned two-year renovation, telling a federal judge in Washington, D.C., that a nonphased approach was chosen to minimize costs and disruptions to operations. “The board’s decisions here were reasonable, and they must stand,” Will Jankowski,…
articles.body:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday defended a decision by the Kennedy Center board to shutter the performing arts center for a planned two-year renovation, telling a federal judge in Washington, D.C., that a nonphased approach was chosen to minimize costs and disruptions to operations.

“The board’s decisions here were reasonable, and they must stand,” Will Jankowski, an attorney in the DOJ’s Civil Division, said minutes into the hearing.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper is weighing a request by the Trump administration to dissolve a preliminary injunction from May that blocked the proposed closure while allowing “necessary maintenance and repair work” to continue.

The judge did not, however, permanently bar the board from ever closing the Kennedy Center “should it come to this decision anew after independently balancing its multiple obligations to the Center in a prudent fashion.”

“It did those things,” Jankowski said, claiming that the board relied on independent assessments from construction firms and real estate experts to make its determination.

President Trump’s handpicked board voted again in September to immediately close the main building for repairs after officials said dilapidated conditions have made it unsafe for visitors.

Public access to the venue was temporarily cut off a day later, a decision Executive Director Matt Floca said in court filings was made after determining there were “acute risks to public safety” due to structural damage in certain parts of the performing arts center.

DOJ lawyers have defended that move as independent of the board’s decision to pursue longer-term renovations.

Lawyers for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), an ex officio board member who’s been leading the charge against Kennedy Center changes, argue that the closure was a cover for financial mismanagement and “foreordained” to please Trump.

“We know that one of the reasons they want to close is because they face fiscal harms and embarrassment as a result of the renaming,” Nathaniel Zelinsky said Thursday.

Several artistic partners ended their affiliations with the Kennedy Center, and a slew of performers canceled or withdrew from shows after the board voted last December to inscribe Trump’s name on the facility. The Washington Post also reported in August that ticket sales and fundraising had plummeted in the months since.

Beatty’s team has also pushed for access to records about Trump’s involvement in the decisionmaking process as chair of the board, a demand the White House has rebuffed by asserting executive privilege over some of president’s communications with advisers and Kennedy Center staff.

Cooper has ordered the Justice Department to turn over copies of those documents to the court by Friday so that he can review them in private and assess the administration’s claim.

He appeared skeptical of both sides’ arguments, at one point asking Zelinsky “what good” it would be to keep the venue open if no performances are scheduled.

“Wouldn’t that cause even more financial deterioration at this point, regardless of who’s to blame for it?” Cooper asked.

The administration, including Trump, has refused to rule out the possibility of razing the building if the president’s name cannot be added and plans for a longer closure are blocked. He was spotted through the window of Air Force One in mid-September looking at a poster board that appeared to say “Kennedy Center DEMOLISH” on it.

“I’m not committing to anything. We’re going to see how it plays out in court,” Trump said in Sept. 28 interview with Time magazine. “But if I build it, and if I agree that for the rest of my life, I’m going to be putting up $100 million to have it open to people … then I think the Trump administration should be recognized.”

The DOJ has suggested in court filings that Trump’s name is inextricably tied to fundraising efforts, while critics argue the president and his allies are attempting to hold the institution hostage.

“The president is putting a gun to the head of the center,” Zelinsky said.

Jankowski argued name recognition for fundraising efforts was “the kind of thing that nonprofits do all the time,” to which the judge responded that was a “different scenario” than alleged in this case.

“Isn’t that more of a form of, you know, taking actions that are contrary to the trust?” Cooper pressed, referencing the assertion that donations could be clawed back if a certain outcome doesn’t happen. “How does that jive with one’s fidelity to the trust?”

The current closure has forced the upcoming Kennedy Center Honors to be moved to an off-site location in the nation’s capital for the first time in its history.

Next month’s ceremony honoring playwright David Mamet, songwriter Paul Anka, composer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia and country music singer Barbara Mandrell is instead being held at Capital One Arena.

Cooper did not issue a ruling from the bench, indicating that he would rule “as soon as” he can.

articles.title: Rufián lanza un dardo a Sánchez tras el cara a cara: “Si Feijóo te come así, es que no te lo has preparado”
articles.standfirst: El portavoz de ERC al Congreso cuestionó la puesta en escena del actual jefe del Ejecutivo
articles.summary: El portavoz de ERC al Congreso cuestionó la puesta en escena del actual jefe del Ejecutivo
articles.body: En la noche de este jueves, 19 de noviembre, se ha celebrado uno de los momentos más esperados de cara a las próximas elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. Ha sido la segunda vez que se han enfrentado cara a cara el actual jefe del Ejecutivo, Pedro Sánchez, y Alberto Núñez Feijóo, del PP. La cita la organizó la Academia de la Televisión en el plató A del Madrid Content City, en Tres Cantos, Madrid y ha sido moderada por la presidenta del mencionado organismo, María Casado. En este contexto, cada uno de los candidatos tenían ocho minutos para hablar en su turno acerca del tema correspondiente. Sin embargo, a la hora de hablar de vivienda o salarios, se vivieron algunos momentos de tensión entre ambos. El presidente del Gobierno afeó al líder de la oposición que no le dejara hablar al interrumpirle en algunas ocasiones. “No me deja hablar. ¿Puedo seguir con mi reflexión?”, dijo Sánchez. El que fuera presidente de la Xunta de Galicia recalcó que solo intentaba “dialogar”. Pues bien, a este momento reaccionó Gabriel Rufián, portavoz de ERC al Congreso, en su cuenta personal de la red social X. El político catalán cargó contra Feijóo y su discurso durante el debate. Además, se pronunció sobre la vivienda y la forma de actuar del jefe del Ejecutivo ante el líder de la oposición. Rufián, en relación a las intervenciones del dirigente de la formación azul, comentó que Feijóo tenía que recordar que era “candidato” y no “tertuliano”: “Los datos y diagnósticos sin propuestas no sirven de nada. Sobre todo, cuando eres uno de los responsables de los mismos”, apostilló. Por otro lado, también se pronunció acerca de lo que Sánchez y Feijóo estaban comentando sobre la vivienda, algo sobre lo que ambos coincidieron: hay que construir más. En este sentido, el portavoz de ERC fue tajante: “Hacer más pisos sin intervenir en el mercado para frenar la acumulación solo sirve para hacer más rico a quien acumula. La falta de valentía en esto arrasará a las izquierdas”. Por último, Rufián cuestionó la puesta en escena de Sánchez durante el debate con el líder de los populares: "Si Feijóo te come así en un debate es que o no te lo has preparado o es que estás mal asesorado. O las dos"

articles.title: Judge rules Trump’s defamation case against New York Times, Penguin Random House may proceed
articles.summary: President Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The New York Times and publisher Penguin Random House can proceed, a federal judge ruled Thursday — a win in the president’s push to paint the news outlet’s reporting about him as misinformation. Trump sued over a 2024 book written by two Times reporters, Russ Buettner and Susanne Craig, and…
articles.body:
President Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The New York Times and publisher Penguin Random House can proceed, a federal judge ruled Thursday — a win in the president’s push to paint the news outlet’s reporting about him as misinformation.

Trump sued over a 2024 book written by two Times reporters, Russ Buettner and Susanne Craig, and published by Penguin Random House. The investigative narrative, titled “Lucky Loser,” recounts the president’s ascent to prominence in the real estate sector.

In the ruling, U.S. District Judge Steven D. Merryday, a former President George H.W. Bush appointee, examined the Supreme Court’s landmark New York Times v. Sullivan ruling — which set the standard for defamation lawsuits. He said that, under this precedent, the president may be able to prove the reporters made knowingly false statements about him.

“Anyone who publishes the claim that someone else has committed a crime of the complex nature described in some of the challenged statements … necessarily proceeds with particularized reason to doubt the truth of their statements and with knowledge of a high degree of probable falsity of the statements,” Merryday wrote.

“In other words, they know that they don’t know, but they are undeterred,” he added.

The Times had sought to dismiss Trump’s claims over the “actual malice” standard for public figures making defamation claims. While ordinary plaintiffs only need to prove a statement’s falsity, lawsuits coming from public figures must also show the respondent acted with the knowledge that what they said was untrue — or acted with a “reckless disregard” for the truth.

In a statement to The Hill, Times spokesperson Charlie Stadtlander vowed to continue to fight Trump’s lawsuit while also praising the judge for dismissing some of his claims

“We continue to believe the remaining claim in the filing has no legal merit. We look forward to making this argument as we continue to defend ourselves against this baseless attack on The Times and the rights of the free and independent press in this country,” Stadtlander said.

Trump has frequently railed against the media throughout his time in and out of office, even briefly barring journalists from accessing White House grounds over their coverage. The president has also sued numerous media organizations for their reporting with mixed success.

His past lawsuits against the Times and Wall Street Journal were dismissed , the former happening in Merryday’s court . Still, he was able to extract settlements out of CBS News and ABC News after his 2024 win and is engaged in another challenge against the BBC , which he similarly accused of libel.

articles.title: Trump’s symbolic summit: From the Politics Desk
articles.summary: In today’s edition, Andrea Mitchell dives into the fallout from President Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting in China.
articles.body: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail. In today’s edition, Andrea Mitchell dives into the fallout from President Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting in China. Plus, Sarah Sternhagen explains why Republicans weren’t far off from suffering even deeper midterm losses. — Adam Wollner Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi was light on results, but heavy on symbolism Analysis by Andrea Mitchell It was an image the White House heralded as historic: an American president holding a summit with the leaders of China and Russia, the three commanders of the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. To some, it had echoes of Yalta in 1945, when Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, and Joseph Stalin divided Europe, with post-war consequences lasting nearly a half-century. This time, substantively, there were no concrete results. But it did send a signal across the globe to see President Donald Trump, the leader of the world’s foremost democracy, standing shoulder to shoulder with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin without even paying lip service to human rights, press freedoms or political prisoners. Afterward, China and Russia issued statements that didn’t dispute the absence of agreements. There was no progress on nuclear proliferation, trade or critical minerals. Trump’s warm embrace with Xi in Shenzhen can be justified by the importance of maintaining a constructive dialogue between the world’s two most powerful economies. Much harder to justify in the eyes of NATO allies is Trump’s affectionate greeting for Putin, calling the invader of Ukraine, “my friend.” Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted on X, “God protect us from such friends.” Perhaps appearing side by side with the two strongmen — both, in effect, leaders for life — was designed to bolster a U.S. president politically weakened by a tsunami-sized midterm defeat, and frustrated by two wars he promised to end quickly. In the case of Ukraine, Trump pledged during the 2024 campaign he could solve the war in one day after taking office. After joining Israel last February in attacking Iran, Trump said the conflict would be over in several weeks. After leaving China, Trump joined a call with his two envoys, Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, who were in Berlin to meet with Ukrainian officials and an eight-member European negotiating team working on security guarantees and an economic reconstruction plan for Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News’ Richard Engel of Trump meeting with Putin and Xi without him, “You can’t decide about some country, even a small country, without this country.” Addressing his nation today, Zelenskyy said the U.S. representatives were going “to provide the necessary information about the U.S. president’s negotiations” and that “we and the Europeans share a clear common position: matters concerning Ukraine must be decided with Ukraine’s participation, and matters concerning Europe must be decided with Europe’s participation.” But prior to the China meeting, European leaders had been assured that Trump, Putin and Xi would not deal with Ukraine without Europe. Punctuating the challenge, Russia attacked Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities during the Shenzhen summit and the hours after. Ukraine drove home its resistance by attacking a key bridge linking Russia with Crimea, a project heavy with strategic and symbolic importance to Putin. Trump recently repeated his belief that Zelenskyy could have prevented the war — apparently ignoring that Putin invaded a sovereign state in violation of past nonaggression pacts. And U.S. negotiators have been pressuring Ukraine for concessions, although Putin has given no indication he is ready to compromise. The Shenzhen summit will likely reinforce the Russian leader’s confidence that he can count on support from Trump. How the blue wave could have been even bigger By Sarah Sternhagen The 2026 elections were already devastating for Republicans, with the party losing a net of at least 42 House seats. But it was close to being much worse for the party. Among the House Republican candidates who managed to win, 26 of them did so by less than 3 points. It’s a number that’s much higher compared to recent midterms, as the chart below illustrates. For instance, in 2018 — another blue wave year — half as many (13) GOP House candidates won their races by less than 3 points. Put another way, only 41 House Republicans won at least 60% of the vote this year. By comparison, more than four times as many (174) House Democrats surpassed that threshold. In the 2022 midterms, when President Joe Biden’s low approval rating weighed down his party, 126 Democratic House candidates still managed to take at least 60% of the vote, while 153 Republicans did. Read more → ☑️ Latest race call: Republican Nick Begich won the race for Alaska’s at-large House district after a ranked choice tabulation, a rare bright spot for his party. That leaves Democrats with 257 seats and Republicans with 173. NBC News’ Decision Desk has yet to project a winner in five remaining House races, including two in Louisiana that are going to December runoffs. That’s all From the Politics Desk for now. Today’s newsletter was compiled by Adam Wollner. If you have feedback — likes or dislikes — email us at politicsnewsletter@nbcuni.com And if you’re a fan, please share with everyone and anyone. They can sign up here.
