articles.summary: Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) hinted at running for reelection in 2028, saying he is “considering things.” “I am considering things,” Fetterman said when MS NOW reporter Mychael Schnell asked if he is going to run in 2028. When the reporter asked if he is worried about a primary challenger in 2028, Fetterman responded saying, “Oh…
articles.body:
Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) hinted at running for reelection in 2028, saying he is “considering things.”

“I am considering things,” Fetterman said when MS NOW reporter Mychael Schnell asked if he is going to run in 2028.

When the reporter asked if he is worried about a primary challenger in 2028, Fetterman responded saying, “Oh … ask [former Rep.] Conor Lamb. What’s he doing?”

Fetterman defeated Lamb in Pennsylvania’s Democratic Senate primary in 2022.

“You have the little guy from Philly. You can ask him why he chickened out,” he added, referring to Rep. Brendan Boyle (D-Pa.), who said he does not plan to challenge Fetterman in 2028, opting instead to remain in the lower chamber where he’s in line to be the next chair of the House Budget Committee.

Fetterman recently said during a Fox News interview that he could leave the Democratic Party if Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is elected as the Senate majority leader, calling it troubling if his “caucus elects someone like Van Hollen that has really made his name being” very hostile to Israel.

Last week, Van Hollen said he would challenge Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for the role of majority leader.

“I think he loses … you’ll have to see how that vote goes,” Fetterman told MS NOW.

While he considers a reelection bid in 2028, multiple candidates are already lining up to possibly challenge Fetterman for his seat. A poll in August showed Fetterman was more popular among Pennsylvania Republicans than Democrats.

Rep. Chris Deluzio (D-Pa.) said Sunday he is seriously considering a 2028 primary challenge against the incumbent Pennsylvania senator, saying, “Fetterman’s been a mess and he doesn’t take the job seriously. Whatever I decide to do, that guy is not going to be the senator in ’28.”

Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American writer, businessperson and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, announced a Senate bid against Fetterman on Nov. 9, less than a week after the midterm elections, where Democrats secured a sweeping victory taking control of both the House and the Senate for the next Congress.

“I’m running to end the war in Iran and to promote the dignity agenda: free healthcare, free childcare, and affordable housing,” Moor wrote on the social plat f orm X .

A day after Moor’s announcement, Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) also said she is considering challenging Fetterman, saying, “I have been concerned about, really, two things, which is his family and his health … and am very disappointed in his activity as a senator and in his votes.”

articles.title: Lawmakers urge Army to postpone Iowa lead detonation, citing late communication
articles.summary: Federal and state lawmakers are urging the Army to postpone its planned detonation of a lead azide bomb in Iowa, citing late communication on the event. “The safety of Iowans now and in the future should be government’s top concern,” Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) wrote on social media. “An unacceptable lack of communication and…
articles.body:
Federal and state lawmakers are urging the Army to postpone its planned detonation of a lead azide bomb in Iowa, citing late communication on the event.

“The safety of Iowans now and in the future should be government’s top concern,” Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) wrote on social media . “An unacceptable lack of communication and clarity has made Iowans understandably concerned and angry about this situation.”

“The public deserves to know, if this is the safest option, why other options were worse,” he continued. “If it isn’t as safe as possible to do this tomorrow, it shouldn’t happen tomorrow.”

The Army announced Nov. 15 in a press release it planned to detonate two degrading lead azide bombs at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant at about noon Nov. 20. Nearby residents were asked to vacate the area from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. local time.

“While safety measures will be fully enforced, the controlled detonation will cause temporary noise, ground vibrations, and a dust plume that will contain some lead,” the release said. “Residents in Middletown will hear a loud noise; feel vibrations from two consecutive, rapid detonations; and will see a plume of dust.”

Sen.-elect Josh Turek (D-Iowa) said he was “deeply concerned” about the detonations, referencing his father’s past exposure to Agent Orange, an air toxin, which led to him being born with spina bifida.

He expressed that it was also “deeply troubling” that there wasn’t prior notice given from the U.S. Army to outgoing Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds (R) or other public officials.

“As I continue to push for answers and reassurances, I am in communication with Senator Joni Ernst and we are doing all that we can to get clarity,” the incoming senator wrote.

Outgoing Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), who lost against Turek for the Hawkeye State’s open Senate seat, similarly remarked that she believed surrounding communities “were not given adequate notice.”

Turek and Hinson both called for Friday’s detonation to be delayed until the impact on local air quality could be studied.

The location of the detonation is just more than 10 miles from the Illinois border, worrying officials in the Prairie State. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker (D) stated on social platform X that his office was monitoring the planned detonation’s effect on nearby Mercer County and surrounding areas.

articles.title: Hawley says he ‘has a lot of thinking to do’ about possible 2028 presidential bid
articles.summary: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) left the door open to a 2028 presidential bid Thursday despite seemingly ruling one out before the midterms. Asked by The Associated Press about a possible run for president, Hawley said he has “a lot of thinking to do.” “After this most recent election, I think everybody that cares about the…
articles.body:
Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) left the door open to a 2028 presidential bid Thursday despite seemingly ruling one out before the midterms.

Asked by The Associated Press about a possible run for president, Hawley said he has “ a lot of thinking to do .”

“After this most recent election, I think everybody that cares about the future of the party, the future of the country, has a lot of thinking to do,” Hawley told the AP. “So, I’ll just say I have a lot of thinking to do.”

The comments about a potential 2028 run come despite his previous remarks to the Washington Examiner in September, when he said he had “no intention of doing so, period.”

Jockeying is already underway for the 2028 primaries on both sides, and the GOP is recalibrating after the party’s brutal midterm losses.

Hawley is one of several Republicans who critiqued the president’s job performance and impact on the midterms. Even Vice President Vance, widely considered a top candidate for the Republican nomination, blamed GOP losses on the Iran war.

The Missouri senator occasionally breaks with his party on more populist issues and recently bashed congressional Republicans for how they handled cost of living issues ahead of the midterms.

“What did we do to get the price of gas down? Nothing. What did we do to get the price of healthcare down? Nothing,” Hawley told reporters on Capitol Hill last week. “I think that this party thought we just do whatever we want … No, you can’t.”

Democrats shut down the government last year in protest over proposed GOP cuts to subsidies for the Affordable Care Act, and Hawley was one of four Republicans to vote with Democrats on an extension, but it ultimately failed.

In recent weeks, he said Republicans should use their remaining weeks in the majority to pass a slate of priority bills, but also a moratorium on data centers, something that has support from populists in both parties.

Talking to reporters last week, Hawley said Congress worked for data centers instead of Americans and said lawmakers received a “F” grade from voters.

“I think that this Congress did not come and work for the people,” Hawley said. “This Congress came and worked for AI companies, and it worked for data centers.”

articles.title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Inside the coordinated activist blitz that crashed Anthropic’s historic Nasdaq debut
articles.summary: As Anthropic rang the Nasdaq opening bell in Times Square, NYPD zip-tied four protesters who blocked the doors with linked arms and pre-printed banners.
articles.body: As Anthropic executives gathered inside the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on Thursday morning to ring the opening bell for a historic $81 billion initial public offering, a tightly orchestrated coalition of far-left, socialist, environmental, anti-Israel and Democratic grassroots groups executed a staged street action outside, complete with linked-arm sit-ins, pre-printed banners and rapid-fire social media drops timed to hijack the news cycle. "This IPO has got to go! Hey, hey, ho, ho," the staged protesters chanted to a small cadre of photographers as the audience. "Shame! Shame!" a protester yelled to a few responding "Shame!" in response. A close look at Thursday’s demonstration reveals the coordinated protest infrastructure that lawmakers have long warned is engineered to "sow discord" rather than produce meaningful policy solutions. According to Fox News Digital's analysis, the protest was no organic, grassroots effort. Rather, 14 groups, several of them part of well-funded organizations with estimated combined annual revenues of $43 million, coordinated the protest with a careful run-of-show and media choreography. A Fox News Digital tracker of the Anthropic protest organizers reveals a well-orchestrated effort across multiple organizations. They represent a spectrum of views from socialists to far-left environmental groups and anti-Israel activists. CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE Advance Setup: 9 AM Call to Arms Roughly 21 hours before the market opened, around 5:45 p.m. EST on Wednesday, the activist network laid the groundwork online, complete with an "Anthropic IPO Day of Action Toolkit" for actions in New York City and the company's San Francisco headquarters, providing ready-made organizing tips to activists with pre-produced graphics, directions to "comment-storm Anthropic's official pages" and "some ideas for signage." In a joint Instagram announcement, posted by Climate Defenders Action and amplified by Climate Defiance and other partner accounts, organizers summoned demonstrators to 43rd Street and Broadway in New York City at 9 a.m. "sharp" on Thursday. Last week, activists from Climate Defiance heckled New York Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, calling him a "traitor." The digital flyer, emblazoned with "STOP AI TECH OLIGARCHS: RALLY AGAINST THE ANTHROPIC IPO," framed the listing as an existential threat to working Americans. Organizers claimed Anthropic was rushing to cash in before an "AI bubble" bursts, arguing that fast-track index inclusion rules would force workers’ 401(k)s and municipal pension funds to buy inflated shares while tech billionaires walk away with billions. The "Day of Action Toolkit" included sign slogan suggestions like "FREEZE AI," the precise language that landed on one sign in New York City. INSIDE THE PROTEST PLAYBOOK TO VILIFY ISRAEL ON 'GLOBAL DAY OF ACTION' ‘Red-Green-Green-Blue’ Coalition The promotional flyer and Instagram collaborator tags reveal a cross-movement coalition spanning socialist, environmentalist, anti-Israel and progressive advocacy groups: FAR-LEFT GROUPS CHEER MAMDANI FOR DISBANDING ELITE NYPD PROTEST TEAM Street Playbook: From Megaphones to Handcuffs On Thursday morning, activists arrived outside Nasdaq’s glass-walled studio at 9 a.m., positioning themselves directly beneath glowing Times Square billboards bearing the ANTHROPIC logo. One masked demonstrator — captioned on screen with his speech about "an IPO" — argued to onlookers and social media cameras that corporations were rushing public offerings to "receive assets" at the expense of everyday workers . ASRA NOMANI: FAR-LEFT US GROUPS BATTLE TRUMP PLAN TO RIVAL CHINA'S TECH DOMINANCE Timestamp Analysis: Engineered for Peak Midday Engagement A review of the organizers' social media shows the coalition staggered its content releases to dominate algorithmic feeds right as Anthropic shares began live trading around midday: The video featured the police van's sirens, fast-cut edits and the staged "perp walk." From the "Action Toolkit," the organizers wrote their own narrative: "Every newspaper and talk show in the world will cover this IPO," the organizers at "Quit GPT" wrote. "If we take action publicly, in the streets, on social media and in Anthropic’s own comments, then this will be swept up in the press story. It could be enough to change the headlines from 'Anthropic delivers best IPO in history' to 'Anthropic IPOs amidst safety outcry.'" A Democratic senator says Republicans are blocking his amendment to ban data centers on public lands as amendment votes on a major permitting reform bill sit in limbo.

In response to a post from a reporter saying that Oregon Sens. Jeff Merkley (D) and Ron Wyden (D) are holding up votes on amendments to the sweeping energy bill, Wyden said that Republicans are blocking his bid to push an amendment that would ban data centers on public lands.

“Republicans are blocking a simple vote on my amendment to ban data centers on public lands. Republicans are too afraid to stand up to Trump even though Americans overwhelmingly voted to rein in data centers,” Wyden wrote on the social platform X.

Merkley’s office confirmed that he, too, is holding up the votes.

A spokesperson for Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) pushed back, saying “Data centers are permitted under state and local law. BAAJA does nothing to change that. It does not authorize a single data center on public lands or anywhere else, and Senator Wyden knows it.”

The Senate on Wednesday teed up its final passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), allowing for 30 hours of consideration in the interim.

A GOP aide told The Hill that senators had been working in good faith to develop a bipartisan list of amendments that could be voted on in the remaining hours, but added that two Democrats were holding up the process. The aide said that the lawmakers could be preventing their colleagues from getting votes on measures that are important to them.

BAAJA more broadly seeks to speed up the nation’s ability to build energy and other infrastructure, including things such as power lines, pipelines and more, in part by reining in the nation’s environmental laws.

Policymakers watch Anthropic IPO with wary eye

Anthropic went public on Thursday, opening with a massive valuation of about $2 trillion . But policymakers were watching with a wary eye, as the AI industry faces a moment of upheaval and uncertainty.

The AI giant raised $81.3 billion in its public debut, making it the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record.

It had priced its shares at $83 on Wednesday night, but began trading at $111.50 , briefly pushing its valuation above $2 trillion.

But this comes at a tumultuous moment as the industry grapples with the recent departure of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, as well as the potentially catastrophic risks from AI — and lawmakers have questions.

Ahead of the IPO, Rep. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.) underscored that the “pressure to deliver profits will be immediate, and it will be immense,” adding that he had “a LOT of questions.”

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) raised concerns that Anthropic has failed to address the “potential threats to Americans’ retirements and the entire financial system if this IPO goes awry.”

And Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) noted the company has “made very, very clear public statements that the technology they’re developing is potentially dangerous” while also moving forward with the IPO. “That makes no sense whatsoever,” he told The Hill.

The cryptocurrency industry is facing a political reckoning as Democrats with a more skeptical view of digital assets prepare to take control of Congress, casting uncertainty about the industry’s legislative prospects.

Two years after securing major campaign and legislative wins, the industry is now facing an uncertain future in DC where new relationships are needed.

This new reality loomed over The Hill and The Block’s Capitol Crypto Forum on Thursday, during which lawmakers and industry leaders signaled a range of attitudes for reviving stalled legislation.

The event fell about two months after the Clarity Act, a major crypto regulation bill, failed to pass the Senate. Insiders agreed chances to revive the effort are low.

But some lawmakers are cautiously optimistic.

Rep. French Hill (R-Ark.), chair of the House Financial Services Committee, pointed to the 78 Democrats who backed the Clarity Act in the House, arguing the industry still has allies in both parties.

Hill told The Hill he was encouraged by a memorandum from Rep. Maxine Waters (D-Calif.), who is hoping to succeed him as chair, outlining digital asset market structure as an issue she intends to work on.

“I’ll blow all your minds. I’ve had conversations with Elizabeth Warren, where she says, ‘I want the industry regulated. I just don’t want the industry to write the regulations,’” Moreno said, praising Warren for being “very, very smart” and “very thorough.”

articles.summary: Presented by Coalition to Strengthen America’s Healthcare {beacon} Healthcare Healthcare The Big Story Intoxicating hemp could snarl government funding A pair of GOP senators say they won’t support any government funding bill if it includes language that delays or reverses the recriminalization of intoxicating hemp products. © AP Photo/Markus Schreiber After bipartisan legislation was introduced…
articles.body:
Intoxicating hemp could snarl government funding

A pair of GOP senators say they won’t support any government funding bill if it includes language that delays or reverses the recriminalization of intoxicating hemp products .

After bipartisan legislation was introduced in the Senate to establish a comprehensive federal regulatory framework for hemp, Sens. Ted Budd (R-N.C.) and Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) strongly objected. In separate social media posts, each said they would not support a government funding bill that overturns a looming ban on most hemp-derived THC products.

“I will not support any year-end package that extends, delays, or builds a regulatory framework around products that fuel addiction, endanger our children, and weaken our workforce,” Budd wrote on X. “Congress closed the hemp loophole more than a year ago to end an industry that never should have existed.”

Budd was responding to a bill introduced this week by Sens. Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.) and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) that would set up a new regulatory framework for hemp products. Among other provisions, it would bar sales of consumable hemp products to people under 21, raise the legal threshold for THC-containing hemp, and ban “gas station” marijuana products derived from hemp.

The legislation’s timing is important. Beginning Dec. 11 , the federal definition of hemp will change to close what critics called the “hemp loophole” brought about by the 2018 Farm Bill, which removed hemp from the controlled substances list.

Without action, hemp industry advocates say their multi-billion-dollar industry could collapse.

Internal Republican disagreements over the issue complicated passage of last funding bill, after a provision delaying the ban for a month was inserted into the legislation. Budd and other senators tried unsuccessfully to get the delay language removed from the bill that Trump most recently signed and are gearing up to try again.

Hemp industry groups and their allies have been lobbying lawmakers to regulate their products, rather than ban them.

“I won’t support any legislation that allows these drugs to continue hurting our kids and communities,” he wrote.

articles.title: From MAGA stardom to a U-Haul: Lauren Boebert considers her own and GOP's losses
articles.summary: Lauren Boebert sat in a U-Haul van in the nation’s capital after packing up her congressional office and her “dungeon of an apartment" on Thursday, about six...
articles.body:
Rep. Lauren Boebert sat in a U-Haul van in the nation's capital after packing up her congressional office and her "dungeon of an apartment" on Thursday, about six years after she became a MAGA star and one week after voters decided not to return her to Washington, D.C.

"I think about it every day," said Boebert, referring to the midterm elections where American voters sent Democrats to Congress en masse. Boebert spoke via Zoom from the van in one of her first interviews since her loss to Democrat Eileen Laubacher in a district Boebert had won by double digits two years ago.

"This could be a referendum on President Trump. It could be the referendum on Congress or the Republican Party," the Colorado Republican said. Then, lowering her voice, she added, "I think it's all of it."

"I'm not mad at the president," she said, but "the president did some things that hurt my voters."

Boebert was one of the most vocal and visible members of the "Make America Great Again" movement, making headlines with her right-wing righteousness on television and the House floor from the time she was first elected, in 2020. Her time in D.C. roughly traced the arc of that movement — and its supporters' more tenuous relationship with Trump of late — through its apogee in 2024 and its more recent midterm losses.

As someone who described herself on Fox News as "ultra MAGA" four years ago, Boebert has become less inclined toward definitions.

"When Jesus comes back and I'm raptured up, like all these labels are just going to fly off anyway," she said. "I respect President Trump, I still work with him, I want to continue to work with him. Not for him, with him."

Boebert says she hasn't changed too much in her six years, besides a few more gray hairs and maybe some "personal growth" on bipartisanship. She said she wouldn't have done anything differently — besides, she joked, "not gone to the theater."

She was referring to an incident at a Denver theater where she was caught on camera vaping at 2023 performance of "Beetlejuice" and escorted out of the venue, a clip that was replayed in campaign ads against her that she partly credits for her loss.

She felt it was an unfair dredging up of a past she'd already "owned up to," but said there could be "a great number of" unaffiliated or Republican voters who, when it came to the scandal, just said, "'I don't care if any of this is true or not, I'm tired of the drama.'"

At the time, she apologized for it up and down her former district, which covered western Colorado. She later moved to a more conservative House seat covering the state's Great Plains, where she won in 2024 before losing two years later. Boebert's opponent raised far more campaign cash than she did.

"I didn't raise millions of dollars and I kinda refused to," she said. "Colorado voters know me, and, you know, if they know me enough to get rid of me, then I guess that's my answer."

Though Boebert has broken from Trump at times — typically on topics other Trump supporters also opposed, such as the war in Iran and the administration's treatment of the Jeffrey Epstein files — she didn't lay the blame for her defeat or other GOP losses squarely at Trump's feet.

"I think it's more all of us. It's all of the Republican Party," she said, citing high gas prices, GOP infighting and unfulfilled promises. "We had solutions and we didn't take action."

Boebert said she doesn't take her loss as an "L," and instead sees it as a "launching pad" for the future, one that she didn't specify but gave a hint toward.

"Too many people come to Congress and get rich," she said. "I am not one of those, and I'm gonna go make some money now."

"The U-Haul is getting started," she said, her camera vibrating a bit as the nation's capital outside the van's window started to move by.

articles.title: House China panel calls for cutting defense contracts over aerospace ties to Beijing's military
articles.summary: A new House report says Airbus and U.S. defense contractors like GE Aerospace and Honeywell should lose taxpayer funds over China aerospace joint ventures.
articles.body: A new congressional report is urging the U.S. to restrict investments in China’s aerospace sector and withhold taxpayer funding from companies that build military capabilities for U.S. adversaries, warning that Western commercial partnerships transferred technology and expertise to Chinese firms with military ties. The 65-page report, titled "China's Wingmen: How Western Government Policy Enabled China's Rise in the Skies," follows a year-long investigation by the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, led by Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Ranking Member Ro Khanna, D-Calif. It examined how legal commercial partnerships transferred advanced technology and manufacturing expertise to Chinese military-linked companies. China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) is the country's military, which the committee says has benefited from civilian aerospace technology transfers. "American and European companies transferred technology to China that could be used against our brave men and women in uniform. With the CCP’s military-civil fusion there are no private companies in China," Moolenaar said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. CHINA COULD EXPLOIT US TECHNOLOGY TO THREATEN AMERICAN FORCES, CONGRESSIONAL WATCHDOG LEADERS WARN "The PLA will exploit civilian technology and use it to advance its military ambitions and that is what happened here." The report singled out European aerospace giant Airbus, which receives U.S. defense contracts while maintaining manufacturing partnerships in China. Although Airbus sold its stake in an AVIC affiliate in 2025, its commercial partnerships with the Chinese aerospace conglomerate continue, according to the committee. The bipartisan panel examined at least six U.S.-China joint ventures involving American defense suppliers GE Aerospace, Honeywell Aerospace and RTX subsidiary Collins Aerospace. Investigators found that GE transferred foundational avionics technology to a joint venture with a subsidiary of AVIC, the Chinese state-owned conglomerate that develops military aircraft, including the J-20 stealth fighter. The committee said GE withheld its original joint venture agreement despite repeated requests. RUSSIA IS HELPING CHINA CLOSE GAP WITH US FORCES AMID TAIWAN TENSIONS, WARNS LONGTIME MILITARY LEADER The American companies maintained that their Chinese partnerships supported civilian aircraft and complied with U.S. export controls. The report also cited previous export-control settlements involving all three companies but did not establish that the partnerships under investigation violated U.S. law. "We appreciate the Committee’s work ensuring the U.S. retains its position as the world’s commercial aviation leader while protecting our most sensitive technologies. We have and will continue to follow relevant U.S. laws and regulations, as the report acknowledges,"a Collins Aerospace spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "GE Aerospace takes national security, compliance, and the protection of its intellectual property seriously, and we work closely with the U.S. government – including this Committee – to ensure we continue to do so," a GE Aerospace spokesperson told Fox News Digital. GE also said its joint venture with AVIC involves older avionics technology sold exclusively in China, not jet engines, and that the arrangement includes safeguards intended to protect sensitive information and ensure compliance with U.S. law. AMERICA'S ENEMIES PREPARE TO TAKE THE NEXT MAJOR WAR INTO OUTER SPACE Honeywell Aerospace told Fox News Digital that its commercial partnerships were fully licensed and approved by the U.S. government, adding that it cooperated transparently with the committee and continues to comply with U.S. export laws. The committee urged the Federal Aviation Administration not to certify Chinese-manufactured aircraft, citing state subsidies and Beijing's refusal to release a final report on the 2022 China Eastern Airlines crash. "The report’s only recommendation directed at the FAA is that they do not certify Chinese-made aircraft, which the agency has not done," an FAA spokesperson told Fox News Digital. articles.title: White House lets go of national cyber director, names acting replacement
articles.summary: Sean Cairncross, the national cyber director, has been let go from his post, a White House official confirmed to The Hill Thursday. The official said President Trump supported the decision to let go of the director, as he believed Cairncross did not have the proper cyber credentials for the job. The Defense Department Chief Information…
articles.body:
Sean Cairncross, the national cyber director, has been let go from his post, a White House official confirmed to The Hill Thursday.

The official said President Trump supported the decision to let go of the director, as he believed Cairncross did not have the proper cyber credentials for the job.

The Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will assume the position in an acting capacity, according to the official, adding that the White House believes she has the credentials for the position. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth congratulated Davies on her appointment as acting national cyber director in a Thursday night post to social platform X — though he did not mention Cairncross.

“Throughout her tenure at DOW, she has proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional, and we are confident she will advance President Trump’s America First agenda across the cybersecurity landscape,” Hegseth added, using an acronym for to the administration’s preferred name for the Defense Department, the Department of War.

Cairncross oversaw the Office of the National Cyber Director, which manages cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. While he played a key role as part of the Trump administration’s AI team, he also reportedly clashed with other arms of the president’s Cabinet.

He allegedly believed the Treasury Department had become too involved with the team’s efforts, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his allies argued Cairncross had not been urgent with responding to questions about AI, according to Axios, which first reported on the departure.

The outgoing director’s head of policy, Thomas Lind, exited his role in June — limiting the number of White House officials with expertise in the emerging technology, the outlet stated. Lind later joined OpenAI in October as head of cyber and strategic risk on its national security policy team.

Cairncross previously served in the White House during Trump’s first term as his chief of staff on National Security Council committees and then led the Millennium Challenge Corporation from 2019 to 2021.

He previously served as the chief operating officer of the Republican National Committee (RNC) from 2015 to 2017 and worked as a senior advisor to former RNC Chair Reince Priebus until 2018.

His departure comes amid growing uneasiness over the potential risks posed by AI, particularly following a series of high-profile attempted or successful hacks on government websites.

It also comes after a rash of tech outages impacted several companies across sectors in recent weeks, one of which caused the Federal Aviation Administration to issue a nationwide ground stop.

The tech issues have caused lawmakers and the public to question whether AI models had caused them. U.S. intel officials, including Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, have denied cyberattacks were behind these outages.

articles.body:
O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), liberou na quinta-feira (19) para julgamento ações que questionam a chamada Lei da Dosimetria , que reduz penas de condenados por atentados golpistas no país. O caso será analisado no plenário virtual entre 4 e 15 de dezembro.

🔎 A lei permite a redução de penas de condenados pelos ataques de 8 de janeiro de 2023, incluindo a pena do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), condenado a 27 anos e três meses de prisão no julgamento da trama golpista, e aliados dele. A lei foi vetada integralmente pelo presidente Lula (PT), mas o Congresso Nacional derrubou posteriormente o veto.

Dados do STF indicam que 455 condenados podem ser beneficiados pela lei da dosimetria, incluindo Bolsonaro . Eles foram condenados por tentativa de abolição do Estado Democrático de Direito e golpe de Estado.

Segundo o tribunal, 200 pessoas permanecem presas , ligadas aos ataques golpistas do 8 de janeiro de 2023 ou à chamada trama golpista que levou à condenação o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL) e aliados.

Segundo o relatório, 183 prisões já cumprem as penas por condenações definitivas. Dessas, 103 são em regime fechado, 3 em semiaberto e 77 domiciliares. Há ainda outras 17 prisões preventivas e 10 prisões domiciliares.

Ministros do STF afirmam de forma reservada que haveria maioria na Corte para manter a dosimetria, com eventuais propostas de ajustes. A aplicação da lei está suspensa desde maio deste ano .

um mecanismo para tornar mais rápida a progressão do regime de pena (quando um condenado sai de uma modalidade mais severa e passa para um regime mais brando) para quem cumpre pena por crimes contra o Estado Democrático de Direito;

redução de até 2/3 da pena imposta aos vândalos comuns dos ataques de 8 de janeiro de 2023;

que o crime de tentativa de golpe de Estado (com penas maiores) vai absorver o de tentativa de abolição do Estado, em caso de condenação simultânea.

A lei impede que as penas desses dois crimes sejam somadas quando ocorrerem no mesmo contexto. Com isso, passa a valer a pena do crime mais grave (Golpe de Estado, de 4 a 12 anos) com um acréscimo de 1/6 até a metade.

Nesta semana, o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), e o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB).

Em maio, o ministro suspendeu a aplicação da lei. Com isso, os condenados pelos atos golpistas de 8 de janeiro de 2023 passaram a depender de uma decisão do plenário para obter o benefício da redução de suas penas.

Moraes aplicou o entendimento a casos de condenados que já haviam acionado a Corte com o pedido de revisão da pena com base na legislação recém-aprovada.

Condenado a 27 anos e três meses de prisão no julgamento da trama golpista, Bolsonaro não chegou a pedir a redução da pena, embora a lei tenha sido articulada por seus aliados e motivada, em parte, pela condenação do ex-presidente.

A defesa do ex-presidente pediu duas vezes a revisão criminal da trama golpista. O procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, já defendeu que o STF rejeite os pedidos . Com o parecer, o ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, relator do caso, já pode levar o caso a julgamento.

A revisão criminal é uma ação que permite contestar uma condenação que já se tornou definitiva, em situações previstas em lei, como diante do surgimento de novas provas.

Ministros ouvidos pelo g1 afirmam que a dosimetria é um caminho alternativo à revisão criminal apresentada pela defesa de Bolsonaro.

Isso porque ela, na prática, diminuiria o tempo de cumprimento da pena de Bolsonaro, aliados e condenados pelos ataques de 8 de janeiro, sem necessariamente criar um novo embate na Corte.

Alexandre de Moraes em sessão plenária do STF — Foto: Antonio Augusto/STF

Aprovação da dosimetria, veto de Lula e retomada do PL

Aprovada em dezembro de 2025, a Lei da Dosimetria permite a redução de penas de condenados pelos ataques de 8 de janeiro de 2023 , incluindo a pena do ex-presidente Bolsonaro e de aliados.

Em janeiro de 2026, o presidente Lula vetou integralmente o projeto de lei. Em abril, o Congresso Nacional derrubou o veto do presidente, retomando os efeitos do PL da dosimetria.

Na Câmara, foram 318 votos favoráveis à derrubada do veto e 144 contrários. No Senado, foram 49 votos para a derrubada do veto e 24 votos contra.

Antes da votação, Alcolumbre adotou uma manobra para evitar conflito com outra lei em vigor. Ele retirou da análise do Congresso um trecho do PL da Dosimetria por contrariar a chamada Lei Antifacção, que havia endurecido regras para progressão de regime.

O trecho retirado pelo presidente do Senado, na prática, facilitava a progressão de regime para condenados por crimes graves, como feminicídio e crimes hediondos.

articles.title: Galípolo diz que ligou para PF para alertar sobre possível fuga de Vorcaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do Banco Central prestou depoimento à Polícia Federal em outubro deste ano no inquérito que investiga a relação de Daniel Vocaro com servidores do BC suspeitos de receber vantagens indevidas e de atuar em favor do Master.
articles.summary: Presidente do Banco Central prestou depoimento à Polícia Federal em outubro deste ano no inquérito que investiga a relação de Daniel Vocaro com servidores do BC suspeitos de receber vantagens indevidas e de atuar em favor do Master.
articles.body:
O presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo , afirmou à Polícia Federal que alertou a corporação sobre a suspeita de que Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, poderia tentar fugir do país.

Em depoimento à Polícia Federal em outubro deste ano, Galípolo disse que o alerta foi feito após o Banco Master pedir, com urgência, uma reunião com o Banco Central em 17 de novembro de 2025, dia da prisão de Vorcaro.

Além disso, o presidente do BC afirmou que informações que eram tratadas em reuniões internas teriam sido vazadas à direção do Master.

"O próprio último pedido de reunião que é feito por parte do banco [Master] pra gente [Banco Central], soa de maneira muito estranha, o que me leva inclusive a fazer uma ligação pra própria Polícia Federal para falar 'olha, tô com receio de que aconteça alguma coisa, porque ele está pedindo uma reunião com uma urgência para agora', o que me pareceu que ele possa estar tentando fugir ou alguma coisa do tipo", afirmou Galípolo em depoimento à PF.

Vorcaro foi preso pela Polícia Federal na noite do dia 17 de novembro de 2025, no Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos, em São Paulo, quando tentava embarcar em um avião particular. A investigação considera que ele tentava deixar o país.

Em depoimento prestado após a prisão, Vorcaro negou que estivesse fugindo.

Disse que a viagem já estava programada e afirmou que havia comunicado ao Banco Central, durante uma videoconferência, que viajaria ao exterior naquele dia . Segundo o banqueiro, a viagem estava relacionada às negociações para a venda do Master a um consórcio com participação de investidores dos Emirados Árabes Unidos.

Horas antes da prisão, Vorcaro e o diretor de Fiscalização do Banco Central, Ailton de Aquino Santos, participaram de uma reunião por videoconferência.

Segundo o relato de Vorcaro à PF, foi nessa reunião que ele informou ao BC que viajaria ao exterior naquele mesmo dia.

Também participaram da reunião Belline Santana, então chefe do Departamento de Supervisão Bancária, e Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza, então chefe-adjunto da área.

A Polícia Federal investiga a atuação dos dois servidores durante o processo que culminou na liquidação do Banco Master, medida adotada pelo Banco Central que retirou a instituição do mercado.

Após a prisão, a defesa de Vorcaro solicitou um documento sobre o encontro e o utilizou no pedido de revogação da prisão preventiva. O documento foi assinado por Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza.

No depoimento, Galípolo afirmou que, ao tomar conhecimento do episódio, determinou que Paulo Sérgio saísse de férias "imediatamente", porque, segundo ele, "a coisa realmente não tinha mais condição de ser tratada como algo simples, tendo ele ultrapassado todos os limites" .

Galípolo também afirmou que o documento encaminhado tinha "conteúdo bastante diferente da prática do Banco Central".

O ofício, datado de 25 de novembro de 2025, registrava informações dadas por Vorcaro ao BC durante a reunião . Segundo o documento, o banqueiro informou que viajaria para Dubai para assinar um contrato com investidores estrangeiros interessados no Master.

"[A certidão feita por Paulo] era muito extensa, a gente não faz atas desse tipo de reunião, não é prática do BC, era uma ata bastante extensa, que dava informações realmente parecendo levantar a bola para esse tipo de entendimento de que 'olha, ele [Vorcaro] tinha um contato, uma solução', foi muito díspar dos documentos tradicionais que o BC produz em ocasiões como essa", afirmou Galípolo.

Gabriel Galípolo, presidente do Banco Central (BC) — Foto: Raphael Ribeiro/Banco Central

Em 28 de novembro, a desembargadora Solange Salgado, do Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região (TRF-1), revogou a prisão.

Na decisão, Solange diz que, "embora inegável a gravidade dos fatos e o vultoso montante financeiro envolvido", a adoção de medidas alternativas à prisão é "suficiente para, atualmente, acautelar o meio social, prevenir eventual reiteração delitiva, garantir a ordem econômica, garantir o regular prosseguimento da persecução penal e coibir o risco de fuga".

Documentos da Polícia Federal divulgados neste ano também mostram que, nos dias anteriores à prisão, Vorcaro enviou mensagens a um número atribuído ao ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal Alexandre de Moraes.

Segundo a PF, foram pelo menos 28 mensagens entre 12 e 17 de novembro de 2025 . Nelas, Vorcaro pediu encontros com Moraes, reclamou de Galípolo e perguntou se o ministro poderia "sensibilizar" o diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues.

Em uma das mensagens, Vorcaro pediu uma tentativa de contato com Galípolo:

"Tentar que o galipolo me receba e eu apresente o que vamos protocolar essa semana. Vamos resolver tudo. Nao podem estourar uma bomba atomica na hora da solucao, nao faz sentido pra ninguem. Nem pra ele, nem pro governo, pra economia e nem para o Brasil."

A mensagem foi enviada em 16 de novembro de 2025, um dia antes da prisão.

Daniel Vorcaro volta a ser preso; Polícia Federal afirma que dono do Banco Master criou uma milícia privada para cometer crimes — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No depoimento à PF, Galípolo também afirmou que houve uma "demora injustificada" de servidores do Banco Central na fiscalização do Master.

Galípolo chegou a afirmar que "esgotou seu repertório de palavrões" ao cobrar a análise do balanço da instituição.

O presidente do BC relatou que passou a aumentar o tom das cobranças diante da demora na produção de análises que considerava relacionadas ao balanço financeiro do banco.

Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza e Belline Santana estão afastados de suas funções no Banco Central desde janeiro deste ano . Segundo a Polícia Federal, os dois atuaram de forma reiterada como consultores informais de Vorcaro, oferecendo orientações, revisando documentos e intervindo em assuntos relacionados à supervisão bancária em favor do Master.

Relatório da PF afirma que Paulo Sérgio orientava Vorcaro em questões relacionadas à supervisão bancária e chegou a revisar a minuta de um ofício que o próprio Banco Master enviaria ao departamento do BC em que ele trabalhava.

Já Belline Santana, segundo a investigação, criou em outubro de 2025 um grupo de mensagens com Vorcaro e Paulo Sérgio para "facilitar nossa interlocução". A PF também identificou mensagens que indicariam pagamentos a Belline. Em uma delas, de outubro de 2024, o valor citado é de R$ 760 mil.

O Banco Central abriu uma investigação interna e sigilosa para apurar a conduta dos servidores.

Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza e Belline Santana, afastados do BC — Foto: Divulgação

articles.title: Pessoas negras representaram 45% dos novos servidores públicos nos últimos quatro anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Percentual supera o mínimo previsto na Lei de Cotas para concursos públicos. Entre 2023 e outubro de 2026, a administração pública registrou 11.543 vínculos a mais de pessoas negras.
articles.summary: Percentual supera o mínimo previsto na Lei de Cotas para concursos públicos. Entre 2023 e outubro de 2026, a administração pública registrou 11.543 vínculos a mais de pessoas negras.
articles.body:
Pessoas negras representaram 45% dos novos ingressos na administração pública federal nos últimos quatro anos. Entre 2023 e outubro de 2026, a administração pública federal registrou 11.543 vínculos a mais de pessoas negras.

Segundo o governo, o percentual de pessoas negras entre os novos ingressos supera o mínimo previsto na Lei de Cotas para concursos públicos porque parte dos candidatos negros também foi aprovada em vagas destinadas à ampla concorrência.

Os dados constam no relatório Retrato da Participação Negra na Administração Pública Federal.

O levantamento foi elaborado pelo Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos com base em informações do Sistema Integrado de Administração de Recursos Humanos (Siape).

Para a diretora da Faculdade de Comunicação da Universidade de Brasília (UnB), Dione Moura, o aumento da presença de pessoas negras no serviço público é positivo e reflete a ampliação do acesso dessa população à educação, especialmente ao ensino médio e superior.

Segundo a pesquisadora, a maior presença de pessoas negras em empregos com estabilidade, como os do serviço público, também pode contribuir para melhorar as condições econômicas do país.

"Mais pessoas negras empregadas e com empregos com maior estabilidade significa mais famílias negras assistidas. Historicamente, no Brasil, a população negra é a que tem menor renda per capita e maior vulnerabilidade social. À medida que mais pessoas negras ingressam no serviço público, temos mais famílias em melhores condições de vida, com mais saúde e segurança", diz.

Apesar do avanço no ingresso, a participação de pessoas negras nos cargos de alta liderança ainda é proporcionalmente menor. Segundo o relatório, o número de ocupantes negros nos níveis 15 a 17 cresceu 59% em quatro anos, passando de 788, em 2022, para 1.254, em outubro de 2026.

No mesmo período, o total de ocupantes desses cargos também aumentou, de 2.663 para 4.103 . Com isso, a participação de pessoas negras na alta liderança passou de 29,6% para 30,6%. O percentual, porém, continua abaixo da média registrada nos demais níveis de liderança.

O levantamento considera cargos de liderança os Cargos Comissionados Executivos (CCE), de livre nomeação, e as Funções Comissionadas Executivas (FCE), destinadas exclusivamente a servidores efetivos.

Na média liderança, o número de ocupantes negros cresceu 23% em quatro anos, passando de 11.740 para 14.455 . A participação dessa população nos cargos subiu de 35,5%, em 2022, para 37,8%, em outubro de 2026.

Para Dione Moura, a desigualdade na ocupação dos cargos de liderança indica que as barreiras enfrentadas pela população negra não terminam com o ingresso no serviço público.

"O fato de não termos muitas lideranças negras, de esse número não ser proporcional, mostra que esbarramos em situações de estigma e barreiras sociais enfrentadas pelas pessoas negras, mesmo depois de conseguirem ingressar no serviço público por mérito e por concurso", afirma.

A pesquisadora defende que gestores públicos reconheçam a qualificação dos servidores negros e ofereçam as mesmas oportunidades de crescimento profissional disponíveis aos demais funcionários.

"Temos que investir em políticas de letramento racial e de redução do preconceito racial. Se você é um gestor público e recebe um servidor negro que passou em um concurso, olhe para esse profissional com os mesmos olhos com que olha para outro servidor que não seja negro. Ele passou por uma bateria de exames, por uma formação anterior e, depois do concurso, por uma formação complementar. Nós, gestores e gestoras, temos que olhar em condições de igualdade para esse servidor e permitir que ele alcance posições de liderança no serviço público", complementa Dione, que foi relatora da política de cotas da Universidade de Brasília.
